signals.title: Duplicate overlapping LLM streams in one session after background task result injection
signals.text: ### Description A real `opencode web` session produced overlapping LLM/provider turns for the same session and the same parent user message. This is not a UI-only duplicate and does not look like an upstream provider retry: the duplicated requests are persisted as distinct assistant messages/parts in OpenCode's SQLite DB and appear as distinct provider usage rows. This appears to be the same bug family as #30809 and #28202, but with additional evidence from provider usage IDs and exact local `session.processor` / `llm.stream` overlap. ### Environment - OpenCode repo/runtime under investigation: `anomalyco/opencode` - Observed runtime version in logs: `1.15.11` - Entry point: `opencode web --port 4096 --hostname 0.0.0.0` - Session: `ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og` - Session directory: redacted user workspace - Model/provider: `openai/gpt-5.5` ### Evidence Two provider usage rows that looked like duplicate requests were confirmed to be real separate requests from the same OpenCode session: - `286185bd-a0c6-4686-a141-43addecd3a61` - OpenCode assistant message: `msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g` - Created: `2026-06-09T08:47:55.397Z` - Finish: `stop` - Tokens: input `861`, cache read `142848`, output `268` - `f9c8faeb-bcba-47a5-8246-1e650d3dd2ea` - OpenCode assistant message: `msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn` - Created: `2026-06-09T08:47:58.850Z` - Finish: `stop` - Tokens: input `629`, cache read `143360`, output `241` Both provider usage rows had: - `request_metadata.client_family = opencode` - session affinity `session=ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og` The local OpenCode DB shows these were not display duplicates. Both assistant messages have real persisted `step-start`, `text`, and `step-finish` parts. Around the same window, several terminal assistant siblings were created under the same parent user message: ```text parent user: msg_eab868be5001ubwGod5Cy16qZo 2026-06-09T08:47:15.458Z msg_eab908402001hktb8SNT9BxEqC finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:24.649Z msg_eab90a7e9001DSqtZTlAxWliH0 finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:35.881Z msg_eab90d3c9001KMOve81qFwnJKU finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:38.347Z msg_eab90dd6b001WlltSckBE8CgPd finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:45.650Z msg_eab90f9f200113JhjG3UT9rB6N finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:55.397Z msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:58.850Z msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn finish=stop ``` The step parts show actual overlap, not just sequential duplicate output: ```text 2026-06-09T08:47:59.889Z step-start msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g 2026-06-09T08:48:03.334Z step-start msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn 2026-06-09T08:48:07.877Z step-finish msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g 2026-06-09T08:48:10.535Z step-finish msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn ``` The service log confirms two prompt-loop sequences were interleaved for the same session: ```text 2026-06-09T08:47:55 service=session.prompt step=40 loop 2026-06-09T08:47:55 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g process 2026-06-09T08:47:55 service=llm ... session.id=ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og ... stream 2026-06-09T08:47:58 service=session.prompt step=39 loop 2026-06-09T08:47:58 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn process 2026-06-09T08:47:58 service=llm ... session.id=ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og ... stream ``` There is an even earlier local log line where the same assistant message ID entered `session.processor process` twice and triggered two `llm` streams: ```text 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=session.prompt step=34 loop 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab90029a001uMQVb8UIKHQtcR process 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=llm ... stream 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab90029a001uMQVb8UIKHQtcR process 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=llm ... stream ``` ### Trigger shape The parent user message was a synthetic background-task completion reminder. The actual project/task content is intentionally redacted, but the structural marker was: ```text <system-reminder> [ALL BACKGROUND TASKS COMPLETE] ... redacted project/task content ... ``` This matches the background result injection path in `TaskTool.injectBackgroundResult`, which forks a parent-session `ops.prompt(...)` when a background task completes. ### Source-path notes Relevant paths in current source: - `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts` - `TaskTool.injectBackgroundResult` calls parent-session `ops.prompt(...)` and forks it. - `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` - `SessionPrompt.prompt()` persists a user message and calls `loop(...)`. - `runLoop()` creates an assistant message and eventually calls `handle.process(...)`. - `loop()` relies on `state.ensureRunning(sessionID, ...)` for same-session serialization. - `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` - `SessionProcessor.process()` logs `process` and calls `llm.stream(streamInput)`. - `packages/opencode/src/session/run-state.ts` - The runner map is an in-memory `Map<SessionID, Runner>` scoped by `InstanceState`. The intended invariant appears to be "one active runner per session", but the evidence above shows that invariant was not held in this session. One likely contributing issue is that `SessionRunState` is not durable; it only protects one in-memory `SessionRunState` instance. If multiple Effect runtime/layer instances or prompt entry points acquire different `SessionRunState` instances for the same session, they can both enter `runLoop()`. The HTTP/server layer also provides `SessionPrompt.defaultLayer` and `SessionRunState.defaultLayer`, while `SessionPrompt.defaultLayer` itself provides a private `SessionRunState.defaultLayer`, which is worth auditing to ensure all prompt paths share the same run-state instance. ### Expected behavior For one session and one parent user/system-reminder message, OpenCode should not run overlapping provider turns or persist multiple terminal assistant siblings unless that is explicitly modeled as separate queued activities. Background task result injection should either coalesce into the active session drain or enqueue a future turn behind a durable/session-owned execution claim. ### Actual behavior Multiple `llm.stream(...)` calls were active for the same session, producing multiple terminal assistant messages under the same parent. This multiplied provider usage and polluted session history. ### Related issues - #30809: very closely related; same-parent duplicate assistant replies around background task result injection. - #28202: closely related; overlapping async/plugin prompts and Web `prompt_async` can create same-parent assistant siblings. - #29478: related duplicate final answers due to fragile prompt-loop completion checks. - #24773: related user-message side of the concurrency gate problem. - #26526: related `promptAsync` fork/context issue; may be relevant if different prompt paths get different instance/run-state context. ### Suggested direction The robust fix should make the session execution claim durable/session-owned rather than only an in-memory `Map` inside one `SessionRunState` instance. At minimum: 1. Audit layer composition so all legacy prompt paths for the same process and instance share exactly one `SessionRunState`. 2. Add regression coverage that simulates background result injection while a parent session drain is active and asserts there is only one provider turn at a time for a session. 3. Consider a DB-backed/session-owned execution lease for legacy sessions, or migrate this path to the V2 durable inbox/coalescing model.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Support drag-and-drop / paste of images in the question tool UI
signals.text: ### Description When the agent invokes the `question` tool (MCQ / structured question UI), there is currently no way to attach images or screenshots while answering. Drag-and-drop and clipboard paste work (or are planned) for the main chat prompt, but the question interface appears to be text/selection-only. This is a common workflow gap: the agent asks a clarifying question, and the user wants to respond with a screenshot (e.g. "which layout do you mean?" → drop a UI screenshot) without dismissing the question modal or switching back to the main prompt. ### Expected behavior While the question tool UI is open, users should be able to: - Drag and drop image files (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP) into the question interface - Paste screenshots from the clipboard (Cmd/Ctrl+V) - See attached images as thumbnails/previews before submitting answers - Have attached images included in the question response sent back to the agent ### Actual behavior - Dropping images onto the question UI does nothing (no dropzone, no attachment) - Pasting a screenshot while focused on the question UI does not attach it - Users must dismiss or work around the question flow and attach images via the main prompt instead ### Motivation / use cases 1. Agent asks "Which error screen are you seeing?" → user drops a screenshot inline 2. Agent asks "Which of these UI variants should we match?" → user attaches reference images 3. Debugging sessions where visual context is faster than describing UI state in text ### Related issues These cover image attach for the **main prompt**, but not the **question tool** UI specifically: - #906 — Feature request: Paste to attach image - #26111 — Windows desktop Ctrl+V + drag-drop - #26780 — TUI drag-and-drop support - #20169 — TUI attach button when drag-drop fails - #18143 — Desktop dropped files in prompt Question tool UI issues (layout/behavior, not image attach): - #31383 — Question Tool popup doesn't appear casually - #11367 — Long question tool makes opencode unusable - #6330 — Generic UI Intent Channel (broader cross-client question UI architecture) ### Suggested implementation notes - Reuse existing prompt attachment / dropzone infrastructure where possible (`prompt.dropzone.label` i18n strings already exist for desktop/web) - Extend the question tool response schema to support optional image attachments per answer or as freeform context - Ensure parity across Desktop, Web, and TUI clients (or document platform limitations) ### OpenCode version Latest (observed June 2026) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session where the agent invokes the `question` tool 2. When the question UI appears, try dragging a PNG/JPG screenshot onto it 3. Alternatively, copy a screenshot to clipboard and press Cmd/Ctrl+V while the question UI is focused 4. Observe that no image is attached and the answer can only be text/selection-based ### Operating System macOS (likely affects Desktop/Web/TUI generally) ### Terminal N/A (Desktop app / question modal)
signals.author: dl-alexandre

signals.title: [FEATURE]: add SSH remote directory references
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Add a new SSH remote directory reference type to opencode's references system. Currently references support local paths and Git repositories only — there is no way to reference files on a remote server without manually copying them or setting up a Git repo. The proposed reference would sync a remote directory via rsync over SSH and make it available as a project reference, following the same async materialization pattern as Git references. #### Proposed config schema: ```jsonc { "references": { "infra": { "host": "devint-229", "remotePath": "/home/devint/infra", "user": "devint", "description": "Infrastructure server" } } } ``` Optional fields: `user`, `port`, `identityFile`, `description`, `hidden`. #### Why rsync? rsync provides incremental sync, delete propagation, and uses the user's existing SSH config (`~/.ssh/config`, ssh-agent) without additional native dependencies (compared to ssh2). #### Implementation status A draft PR with a complete implementation is available: **https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/31900** The implementation includes: - `SshSource` as a new variant in the `Source` tagged union - `ConfigSsh` config schema class - rsync-based cache service with EffectFlock locking - Input validation and non-interactive SSH host key handling - Tests and documentation
signals.author: heitorfreitasferreira

signals.title: Per-model npm override in custom provider config is ignored
signals.text: ### Description When configuring a custom provider with a per-model `npm` override (as documented in the Providers page under "Troubleshooting"), the override is silently ignored. The provider-level `npm` package is always used regardless of model-level overrides. ### Use case We run a LiteLLM proxy that serves both Claude (via Bedrock) and GPT (via Azure). LiteLLM exposes both `/v1/messages` (Anthropic-native) and `/v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI-compatible) on the same endpoint. We need Claude models to use `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (→ `/v1/messages`) and GPT models to use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (→ `/v1/chat/completions`) under a single provider. ### Configuration ```json { "provider": { "litellm": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/anthropic", "options": { "baseURL": "https://litellm.example.com/v1", "apiKey": "{env:LITELLM_VIRTUAL_KEY}" }, "models": { "claude-sonnet-4-6": { "name": "Claude Sonnet 4.6" }, "azure/gpt-4-1": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "name": "GPT-4.1" } } } } } ``` ### Expected behavior - `litellm/claude-sonnet-4-6` → uses `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (provider default) - `litellm/azure/gpt-4-1` → uses `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (per-model override) ### Actual behavior Both models use the provider-level `@ai-sdk/anthropic`. The per-model `npm` field is ignored. Also tested the inverse (provider default `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, Claude models with `"npm": "@ai-sdk/anthropic"` override) — same result: override ignored. ### Documentation reference The [Providers docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers) state under Troubleshooting: > "For mixed setups under one provider, you can override per model via `provider.npm`." ### Workaround Define two separate providers with different `npm` packages: - `litellm` with `@ai-sdk/anthropic` for Claude models - `litellm-gpt` with `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` for GPT models ### OpenCode version 1.17.1 ### Operating System macOS

signals.title: [BUG]: Skill discovery logs false "duplicate skill name" warnings when .claude/skills is a symlink to .agents/skills
signals.text: ## Description A common multi-agent convention is to keep one canonical skills directory and symlink the agent-specific paths to it, e.g.: ``` .agents/skills/ # canonical, shared by Claude Code / Codex / opencode .claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills ``` opencode scans both `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, does not resolve symlinks to a real path, and therefore discovers every skill twice — logging a `WARN duplicate skill name` per skill on every startup: ``` timestamp=2026-06-12T02:16:25.049Z level=WARN run=1285e688 message="duplicate skill name" name=demo-skill existing=/tmp/oc-symlink-repro/.claude/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md duplicate=/tmp/oc-symlink-repro/.agents/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md ``` In a project with ~30 skills this produces ~30 warnings per session start, drowning out real log signal. Note this is **not** the case fixed in #26709 — there the `existing` and `duplicate` paths were *identical strings*. Here the paths are different strings pointing at the same physical file through a symlinked directory, so the string-equality skip does not apply. #17219 reports the same root cause (no realpath dedup) in the permission scanner. ## Steps to reproduce ```bash mkdir -p repro/.agents/skills/demo-skill repro/.claude cat > repro/.agents/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md <<'SKILL' --- name: demo-skill description: Demo skill for symlink dedup repro --- Demo body. SKILL ln -s ../.agents/skills repro/.claude/skills cd repro && git init -q opencode run 'hi' # then check the log: grep 'duplicate skill name' ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | grep demo-skill ``` ## Expected behavior Skill files reachable through more than one scan path should be deduplicated by resolved real path (`fs.realpath`) and produce no warning. Alternatively (or additionally) a config option to restrict skill discovery directories (#23035) would let users opt out of scanning one of the locations. ## Environment - opencode 1.17.3 (also reproduced on earlier 1.17.x) - Linux x86_64 (NixOS), opencode installed via nix

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Allow filtering/scoping MCP resources in the @ autocomplete menu
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request **Summary:** Provide a way to filter/disable (or scope) **MCP resources** in the `@` autocomplete menu. Today every resource advertised by every connected MCP server is injected, unbounded and unfilterable, into the same `@` list as project files — so a single resource-heavy server can drown out file completion. **Concrete trigger:** The Datadog MCP server (`@datadog/opencode-plugin` + its remote MCP) advertises its skill catalog as ~70 MCP **resources** (`datadog/logs`, `datadog/traces`, `datadog/rum`, ...). After connecting it, typing `@` floods the file selector with these `datadog/*` entries, making it hard to reference actual files/folders. **Where this happens (source):** In `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx`, the `@` menu is assembled from files + reference aliases + agents + **all MCP resources**, with no per-source filter and no cap: ```ts // autocomplete.tsx (~L480-481) const nonFileOptions: AutocompleteOption[] = store.visible === "@" ? [...referenceAliasesValue, ...agentsValue, ...mcpResources()] : [...commandsValue] ``` ```ts // autocomplete.tsx (~L355-389) — every resource from every server, unconditionally const mcpResources = createMemo(() => { if (!store.visible || store.visible === "/") return [] const options: AutocompleteOption[] = [] for (const res of Object.values(sync.data.mcp_resource)) { // ...pushed into the @ list with no filtering } return options }) ``` **Why this is an opencode gap (not the server's):** The MCP spec leaves resource UX entirely to the client. opencode already gives users this kind of control for **tools** (the `tools` glob, e.g. `"mymcp_*": false`, documented under MCP servers → Manage) and for file-based **skills** (`permission.skill` patterns). MCP **resources** have no equivalent escape hatch — they cannot be filtered globally, per-server, or per-agent, and there's no `@`-source scoping. A server acting within convention can therefore make `@` unusable for files, and the user has no recourse short of disabling the whole MCP server (`mcp.<name>.enabled: false`), which also kills that server's tools. **Desired behavior (any one of these would resolve it):** 1. **Glob filter for resources**, mirroring the existing `tools` mechanism — e.g. allow `tools`/a new `resources` glob to suppress a server's resources: `"datadog_*": false` or `"resources": { "datadog/*": false }`. 2. **Per-server toggle** to exclude a server's resources from `@` while keeping its tools, e.g. `mcp.<name>.resources: false`. 3. **Source-scoping for `@`** — let users restrict (or visually separate) what `@` lists, e.g. files-only vs. files + agents + references + resources, via config or a keybind, instead of one merged ranked list. 4. At minimum, an **upper bound / lazy grouping** for resources in `@` (related to the unbounded-enumeration concern in #29462 for skills), so one server can't dominate the list. Option 1 or 2 is the most consistent with existing opencode conventions for tools. **Environment:** - opencode version: 1.17.3 - Repro server: Datadog MCP (`@datadog/opencode-plugin`, remote MCP at `mcp.datadoghq.com`), which exposes its skill catalog as MCP resources. **Related (not duplicates):** - #27979 — group skills by colon-separated prefixes (display grouping; doesn't add filtering and is about skills, not MCP resources) - #29462 — skills tool enumerates all skills with no upper bound (same "unbounded, no `hidden`/cap" shape, but for the `skill` tool / system prompt, not MCP resources in `@`) - #29189 — `hidden` frontmatter for skills (analogous "let me hide entries" ask, for file skills) - #15535 / #14753 — about *supporting/reading* MCP resources, not curating them out of the `@` menu

signals.title: Task panel static - does not update in real time (Windows)
signals.text: ## Bug Description The task panel (using \ odowrite\ tool) remains static and does not show changes in real time across all projects. This affects: - Task list updates - File tree changes - Changes panel - Subagent responses ## Environment - **OS**: Windows 11 - **OpenCode Desktop Version**: Latest (as of 2026-06-14) - **Shell**: PowerShell 7+ - **Platform**: win32 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create tasks using \ odowrite\ tool 2. Update task status (pending → in_progress → completed) 3. Observe that the task panel does not reflect changes 4. Switch to another session and back - changes appear 5. Or restart OpenCode Desktop - changes appear ## Expected Behavior The task panel should automatically refresh within a few seconds when tasks are modified, similar to how modern IDEs update their UI. ## Actual Behavior The task panel remains static until: - User switches sessions - User restarts OpenCode Desktop - User performs some action that triggers UI refresh ## Related Issues This issue is related to multiple existing issues: - #28393: File refresh not working - #23321: Changes panel does not update when files are modified externally - #22134: File view requires restart to show newly created files - #17654: Remote server responses not updating in desktop app ## Impact This bug significantly impacts workflow efficiency because: 1. Users cannot see real-time progress of tasks 2. Subagent results are not immediately visible 3. File changes require manual refresh or restart 4. Multi-step workflows become difficult to track ## Suggested Fix The file watcher system using SSE events (\ ile.watcher.updated\ → \ efreshVcs()\) may not be arriving reliably in the desktop app. Consider: 1. Adding a manual refresh button for the task panel 2. Implementing periodic auto-refresh (e.g., every 5 seconds) 3. Ensuring SSE events are properly received by the frontend 4. Adding keyboard shortcut for manual refresh (e.g., Ctrl+R) ## Additional Context This issue affects all OpenCode Desktop users on Windows and potentially other platforms. The web interface does not have this problem.

signals.title: Bug: opencode run processes don't exit after completing scheduled work, causing memory leak
signals.text: # Bug Report: `opencode run` processes don't terminate after completing scheduled work **OpenCode version:** 1.17.6 **Platform:** macOS (also affects Linux via the same supervisor.pl scheduler) **Severity:** High — memory leak in scheduler cron jobs ## Summary When `opencode run` is executed as a scheduled cron job via the built-in scheduler (`supervisor.pl`), the Node.js process does not exit after completing its prompt. The process remains alive indefinitely with an idle event loop (stuck on `kevent64` syscall), consuming 90–400 MB RSS each. Over days, orphaned processes accumulate with PPID=1 (re-parented to launchd), consuming all available RAM. ## Root Cause 1: `opencode run` doesn't call `process.exit()` After completing the scheduled prompt, the Node.js runtime stays alive because active handles (SQLite connections to `opencode.db`, timers, unix sockets) keep the event loop running. The process sits idle on `kevent64()` waiting for I/O events that never come. **Evidence from `sample` of PID 1942 (email check, 14 hours running):** ``` Call graph: 4240 Thread_4497486 + 4240 start + 4240 ... main thread + 4240 ... kevent64 (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) ``` 100% of CPU samples show the main thread blocked on `kevent64` — the Node.js event loop waiting for work that will never arrive. **lsof evidence:** ``` FD 7 → opencode.db (3 GB WAL) FD 8 → opencode.db-wal (2.6 MB) FD 13 → unix socket FD 22 → unix socket FD 26 → unix socket FD 28 → unix socket ``` Open SQLite connections and unix sockets prevent the event loop from exiting. ## Root Cause 2: `supervisor.pl` uses `setsid()` which orphans children The scheduler supervisor script calls `setsid()` in the forked child process (line 178 of supervisor.pl): ```perl if ($child_pid == 0) { chdir $workdir or die "..."; eval { setsid(); }; # <-- creates new session, detaches from parent exec { $command } $command, @args; } ``` This creates a new session, detaching the child from the parent process. When `opencode run` doesn't exit, the supervisor is stuck in `waitpid()`. If the supervisor is killed (e.g., by system OOM or launchd timeout), the child survives because it's in its own session and re-parents to PID 1. Without `setsid()`, the child would receive SIGHUP when the parent dies, preventing orphan accumulation. ## Root Cause 3: Timeout misses sub-processes The alarm handler sends SIGTERM/SIGKILL to `-$child_pid` (the process group), but `opencode run` spawns sub-processes (MCP servers) in different process groups, so they survive the kill and become orphans. ## Reproduction Steps 1. Schedule any `opencode run` command via the scheduler: ``` opencode schedule --name test-job --schedule "0 * * * *" --prompt "echo hello" ``` 2. Wait for the job to execute 3. Observe that the process persists after the work completes: ``` ps aux | grep "opencode run" ``` 4. After multiple schedule intervals, orphaned processes accumulate with PPID=1 ## Impact - Each orphan consumes 90–400 MB RSS - 16+ orphans observed consuming ~2.5 GB total - System enters memory pressure (31/32 GB used) - Additional OOM killing of legitimate processes - Scheduler lock mechanism prevents new jobs from starting while old ones (incorrectly) hold the lock ## Suggested Fix (in opencode binary) `opencode run` should call `process.exit(0)` after the prompt completes and all output is flushed. Specifically: 1. Ensure all database connections are closed after the run completes 2. Call `process.exit()` explicitly rather than relying on the event loop to drain ## Suggested Fix (in supervisor.pl — workaround) Replace `setsid()` with `setpgid(0, 0)` to keep the child in the same session so it dies with the parent. Add recursive process tree killing for timeout handling. Add pre-flight orphan cleanup. (Implemented locally at `~/.config/opencode/scheduler/supervisor.pl`.) ## Workaround Script A cleanup script is available at `~/.config/opencode/scheduler/cleanup-orphans.pl` that kills any `opencode run` process older than 1 hour with PPID=1.
signals.author: m-faizan-tariq

signals.title: TUI: incomplete terminal teardown on exit — mouse tracking, alt-screen, bracketed paste left enabled
signals.text: ### Description When OpenCode TUI exits (via `/exit`), several terminal features that were enabled at startup are **not** disabled. This leaves the terminal in a broken state: mouse movements print garbage characters (numbers/escape codes), bracketed paste is stuck on, and the alternate screen buffer may not be properly restored. The only fix is to manually run `reset` or close and reopen the terminal window. **Environment** - **OpenCode version:** latest (installed via `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`) - **OS:** Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04) - **Terminal:** Windows Terminal - **Shell:** bash 5.2 **Plugins** `@opencode-ai/plugin: "1.17.1"` (in `.opencode/package.json`). **OpenCode version** 1.17.6 **Steps to reproduce** 1. Run OpenCode in any project: `opencode .` 2. Send a message to the agent, wait for a response. 3. Exit via `/exit` (not Ctrl+C — clean exit). 4. signals.title: bug: worktree creation fails on empty repos with '--orphan and --no-checkout cannot be used together'
signals.text: ## Issue 當在一個「空 Git 倉庫」（已 `git init` 但尚未有任何提交記錄）上新增工作區時，建立失敗。 ## 錯誤訊息 ``` 建立工作區失敗 No possible source branch, inferring '--orphan' fatal: options '--orphan' and '--no-checkout' cannot be used together ``` ## 重現步驟 1. 在一個目錄執行 `git init`（但不進行任何 commit） 2. 在 opencode.app 中使用該目錄建立工作區 3. 觀察到上述錯誤 ## 根因分析 當 `git worktree add` 找不到可使用的來源分支時，會自動推斷 `--orphan` 選項。 但 opencode 在呼叫時同時傳遞了 `--no-checkout` 參數。 這兩個選項互相矛盾： - `--orphan` 要求檢查出工作樹（否則孤兒分支沒有歷史起點） - `--no-checkout` 要求不要檢查出工作樹 Git 無法同時滿足這兩個條件，導致失敗。 ## 目前繞過方法 先在該目錄建立一個初始提交： ```bash touch .gitkeep git add .gitkeep git commit -m "Initial commit" ``` ## 建議修復 在 `packages/opencode/src/worktree/` 中，當 repo 處於 empty/unborn HEAD 狀態時： - 不要同時傳遞 `--orphan` 和 `--no-checkout` - 或者先檢查 repo 狀態，對空倉庫採用不同的建立策略 ## 環境 - opencode 版本：1.17.6 - 作業系統：macOS (darwin arm64) - Git 版本：系統預設 ## 相關 Issue 這與 #20910（application can't handle git repos with no head）可能相關，但此 issue 提供更具體的錯誤細節和 Git 選項衝突分析。

signals.title: ACP sessions can leave supplied MCP servers registered after close
signals.text: ### Description When an Agent Client Protocol (ACP) client opens an OpenCode session with MCP servers in `mcpServers`, OpenCode registers those servers on the instance. After the ACP session is closed, the ACP session state is removed, but the MCP server registration can remain. That seems surprising because the MCP server came from the ACP session request. If this is intentional, the ownership rules are not obvious. With repeated ACP session churn, this can leave extra MCP state around and may be related to the broader memory growth discussion in #20695. Expected behavior: An MCP server supplied only by one ACP session should be cleaned up when that ACP session closes. If the same MCP server is still used by another open ACP session, it should stay available until the last owner closes. Actual behavior: The ACP session can close while its supplied MCP server remains registered in the OpenCode instance. ### Plugins None required. This uses MCP servers supplied by an ACP client through `mcpServers`. ### OpenCode version 1.17.7, also reproduced on current dev commit `a774c62ea` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open an ACP session with one `mcpServers` entry, for example a local server named `tools`. 2. Confirm the OpenCode instance registers that MCP server for the session. 3. Close the ACP session. 4. Check whether the MCP server is still registered for the instance. In a direct reproduction against dev commit `a774c62ea`, opening three ACP sessions with two MCP servers each registered six MCP servers. Closing those sessions did not perform any corresponding unregister or cleanup calls. ### Screenshot and/or share link None ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal / PowerShell

This causes the UI to show "file listing failed" for the project. The expected behavior is that missing subdirectories should be gracefully skipped — the listing should continue for the remaining entries instead of crashing. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. signals.title: Desktop upgrade can fail on workspace migration
signals.text: ## Description Upgrading some older desktop installs can fail during database migration with: ```text no such column: name ``` The failing path is `20260410174513_workspace-name`. It rebuilds the `workspace` table and copies `workspace.name`, but some upgraded databases have a legacy `workspace` shape that already has `type`, `directory`, and `extra` while still missing `name`. Minimal repro: https://github.com/neriousy/opencode-workspace-migration-repro The repro now includes copied opencode migration file versions under `opencode-migrations/` and executes the copied `20260410174513_workspace-name/migration.sql` for the failing case. Suspected origin: - `7f37acdaaa89b358fb795ccd006d37ed7fa6672e` (`feat(core): rework workspace integration and adaptor interface`, package version `1.2.16`) added `20260303231226_add_workspace_fields/migration.sql`, which normally adds nullable `workspace.name`. - `bf50d1c028e973ccc0beffdf568fca417b62f020` (`feat(core): expose workspace adaptors to plugins`, package version `1.4.3`) added `20260410174513_workspace-name/migration.sql`, whose copy step assumes `workspace.name` already exists. - `7f571d36ea56cc3dd7059cfe82c729fb52b121eb` (`refactor(core): move database schema ownership`, package version `1.15.13`) moved the migration into `packages/core/src/database/migration/20260410174513_workspace-name.ts` with the same `SELECT name` assumption. Builds containing this path can surface the older assumption during upgrade. - Proposed fix is mirrored in the repro at `opencode-migrations/20260410174513_workspace-name/proposed-fix.ts`. ## Plugins N/A ## OpenCode version Observed in newer desktop upgrades; suspected affected line starts with builds containing `7f571d36` / package version `1.15.13`, with the unsafe migration originally introduced in `1.4.3`. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Clone https://github.com/neriousy/opencode-workspace-migration-repro. 2. Run `bun run repro`. 3. The copied opencode SQL migration fails while selecting `name` from `workspace`, then the proposed fix path succeeds. ## Screenshot and/or share link https://github.com/neriousy/opencode-workspace-migration-repro ## Operating System Desktop, observed during upgrades from older installs. ## Terminal N/A

signals.title: [BUG] Stuck subagents can't be nudged/restarted — Esc+Esc creates contextless replacement
signals.text: ### Description When a subagent's LLM stops responding (gets stuck — happens with various models/providers, especially on long-running tasks), there is no way to nudge or retry within the existing subagent session. **The main-agent workaround doesn't work for subagents:** For the main agent, when the LLM stops responding, you can press Esc Esc to cancel and then type `cont` — the agent resumes with full context. This is a well-known and effective workaround. For subagents, this **doesn't work**: 1. Esc Esc cancels the stuck subagent 2. Typing `cont` causes the main agent to interpret the cancellation as "subagent is done" 3. The main agent spawns a **brand new subagent** with zero context of the previous one's work All accumulated tool calls, file reads, and reasoning from the stuck subagent are lost. The parent agent has no access to the partial results. This is especially painful when the subagent has been running for a long time (10+ minutes of exploration) and gets stuck near the end. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Launch a subagent that does substantial work (e.g., multi-file exploration with many tool calls) 2. Wait for the subagent to get stuck (LLM stops responding — reproduces with models that have connection issues or rate limiting) 3. Press Esc Esc to cancel the stuck subagent 4. Type `cont` to try to resume 5. Main agent creates a new subagent from scratch — previous subagent's session and work are inaccessible to both the user and the parent agent ### Expected behavior At minimum one of: - **Nudge/retry**: ability to retry the last LLM call within the same subagent session, preserving full context - **Resume after cancel**: cancelled subagent sessions should be viewable (related: cancelled subagents can't be opened in TUI) and their partial results should be available to the parent - **Explicit restart**: ability to restart a subagent within its existing session/context rather than spawning a fresh one ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal TUI ### Related issues - #30711 — subagent watchdog/timeout mechanism (automated detection; this issue is about manual recovery) - #29209 — Interrupted subagents lose completed work/context (same data-loss symptom) - #23415 — Whole workflow stalls if any sub-agent is aborted

signals.title: [BUG] Cancelled subagents can't be opened in TUI + Ctrl+X intermittently fails
signals.text: ### Description Two related subagent navigation issues in the TUI: **Part A — Cancelled subagents become inaccessible:** While a subagent is **running**, clicking on it in the TUI navigates to its session view — you can watch its progress, tool calls, and output. But once the subagent is **cancelled** (e.g., via Esc Esc), clicking on it does nothing. The session transcript becomes completely inaccessible from the TUI. This is problematic because you often want to cancel a subagent that's gone down the wrong path, then inspect what it found before discarding it. Currently there's no way to do this. **Part B — Ctrl+X (agent/session switcher) intermittently fails:** Ctrl+X sometimes doesn't open the picker at all. No error, no feedback — it just does nothing. Haven't been able to identify a reliable pattern for when it fails vs works. When it does work, the picker shows subagent sessions but the reliability issue makes it an unreliable workaround for Part A. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce **Part A:** 1. Launch a subagent (e.g., via the task tool — `task(subagent_type="explore", ...)`) 2. While it's running, click on the subagent row — you can view its session ✓ 3. Cancel the subagent with Esc Esc 4. Click on the now-cancelled subagent row 5. Nothing happens — the session is inaccessible ✗ **Part B:** 1. During an active session with or without subagents, press Ctrl+X 2. Sometimes the picker appears, sometimes it doesn't 3. No consistent trigger identified ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal TUI

signals.title: [BUG] Severe tool call lag / slow thinking / UI freeze / page display slowness in large repos (100GB+, 1M+ files) — 大型仓库工具调用卡顿、思考慢、页面卡死、展示延迟
signals.text: ### 中文部分 **问题现象：** 在 157GB、100 万+ 文件的大型 Unity 仓库中，OpenCode 每次工具调用（grep / read / edit 等）感知延迟高达 15~20 秒，长会话后更严重。表现为"模型思考慢"、"页面卡住不动"、"工具执行很久才有结果"。 **根因分析：** 通过源码级链路追踪发现，**卡顿主因不是模型推理慢**，而是 OpenCode 在每次工具调用周期内（`processor.ts` 的 step-start → tool.execute → step-finish）会执行 4 次 `snapshot.track()`，每次内部 fork 4~5 个 git 子进程（`diff-files`、`ls-files --others`、`check-ignore`、`add --all`、`write-tree`），在 23.8 万跟踪文件 + NTFS 上单次耗时约 4 秒，合计 **~16 秒/次工具调用**。次要原因包括：File Watcher 事件风暴（Unity Library 目录高频变更）、Ripgrep 搜索扫描 100 万文件范围过大、`.ignore` 未配置导致搜索无法跳过大型二进制目录。 **处理方案（5 步，不改源码）：** 1. **关闭 Snapshot**：`opencode.json` 加 `"snapshot": false`，单次工具调用节省 ~16 秒（官方 @thdxr 也建议过此方案）。失去 undo 功能，可用 `git stash` 替代。 2. **创建 `.ignore` 文件**：ripgrep 原生支持的 ignore，列出 Library/Temp/build 等大型目录，搜索提速 3~5 倍，不影响 git。 3. **完善 `watcher.ignore`**：在 `opencode.json` 中配置 90+ 条规则，阻止 Unity 缓存目录触发事件风暴。 4. **补全 `.gitignore`**：排除 HybridCLR/Wwise 等构建产物（需团队确认）。 5. **优化 `.opencode/.gitignore`**：防止本地配置泄露到 git。 综合收益：每次工具调用从 ~20 秒降至 < 2 秒，搜索提速 3~5 倍，长会话不再累积延迟。 --- ### English part **Symptom:** In a 157GB Unity repo with 1M+ files, every tool call (grep/read/edit) takes 15-20 seconds. The UI feels frozen, "thinking" appears to stall, and page rendering is sluggish — especially in long sessions. **Root Cause:** Source-level tracing reveals the bottleneck is **not model inference**, but OpenCode's **snapshot subsystem**. Each tool call cycle (`processor.ts`: step-start → execute → step-finish) triggers `snapshot.track()` **4 times**. Each `track()` forks 4-5 git sub-processes (`diff-files`, `ls-files --others`, `check-ignore`, `git add --all`, `write-tree`). On 238K tracked files over NTFS, a single track takes ~4s, totaling **~16s per tool call**. Secondary causes: File Watcher event storms from Unity's `Library/` dir, Ripgrep scanning 1M files without `.ignore`, and unbounded SSE event queues (related to #20695, PR #31922). **Solution (5 steps, no source code changes):** 1. **Disable snapshot**: Add `"snapshot": false` to `opencode.json`. Saves ~16s per tool call. Loses undo — use `git stash` instead. (Also recommended by maintainer @thdxr in #20695.) 2. **Create a `.ignore` file**: ripgrep's native ignore — list heavy dirs (`Library/`, `Temp/`, `build/`, etc.). Speeds up grep/glob/find by 3-5x. Does not affect git. 3. **Configure `watcher.ignore`**: Add 90+ rules in `opencode.json` to prevent Unity cache dirs from triggering event storms via `@parcel/watcher`. 4. **Improve `.gitignore`**: Exclude build artifacts (HybridCLR, Wwise sound banks, etc.). Requires team coordination. 5. **Optimize `.opencode/.gitignore`**: Prevent local OpenCode config from leaking into git tracking. **Combined result**: Tool call latency drops from ~20s to < 2s. Search speeds up 3-5x. No more cumulative lag in long sessions. --- **Related issues:** #20695, #24771, #30101, #28702, #32409

signals.title: Desktop sidecar crash: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN (0xC0000409 / exit 3221226505) from @parcel/watcher std::regex_match on long paths (upstream parcel-bundler/watcher#250)
signals.text: ### Summary On Windows, the OpenCode Desktop sidecar process crashes with exit code `3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`), taking the local server offline and making the conversation unresponsive. Forensic analysis of the Windows minidump points the crash at the bundled native file-watcher module `@parcel/watcher-win32-x64\watcher.node`. The crash is triggered when the watcher's glob/regex engine processes very long filesystem paths, matching the known upstream bug `parcel-bundler/watcher#250`. This looks like the same crash class as #29033 (open) and #28413 (closed) — both report the identical exit code on Windows, but neither pinpointed the underlying module. This report adds the minidump-confirmed root cause and the upstream link. ### Environment - **OpenCode version:** Desktop **v1.17.7** (Windows x64) - **Operating System:** Windows 11 (10.0.26100) - **Terminal:** desktop - The crash is **not** model-specific — it was observed across multiple models. The trigger is the filesystem path, not the AI model. ### Symptoms | Symptom | Detail | |---|---| | UI | Local server disconnects; conversation becomes unresponsive | | Sidecar exit code | `3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`) | | Logs | `sidecar exited { code: 3221226505 }` | | Reproducibility | Deterministic when long paths are written inside the watched workspace | ### Root cause (minidump evidence) A Windows crash dump is generated under: ``` %APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\Crashpad\reports\ ``` Key facts from the dump: | Field | Value | |---|---| | Exception code | `0xe0000008` (fast-fail / stack-buffer-overrun family) | | Exception location | inside `KERNELBASE.dll` | | Loaded native module | `@parcel\watcher-win32-x64\watcher.node` | The stack overflow originates in the watcher's native code — not in the Node application logic or in user scripts. It matches the known upstream issue: > Stack overflow crash (`STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` / `0xC0000409`) in `std::regex_match` on long paths when using a glob ignore option — `parcel-bundler/watcher#250` `@parcel/watcher` applies `std::regex_match` to filesystem paths; with sufficiently long input strings the regex engine consumes enough stack space to trip the compiler `/GS` buffer-security check. The crash is therefore path-length dependent. ### Steps to reproduce > **Warning:** this will disconnect the OpenCode session. Run only in a disposable workspace. Create a file with a very long basename inside a directory that OpenCode is watching: ```powershell $dir = "C:\some\watched\workspace" $long = "VERY_LONG_BASENAME_" + ("x" * 200) + "_20260101T000000Z.txt" Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $dir $long) -Value "test" ``` A deep directory hierarchy combined with a very long basename (total path well beyond 260 characters) reliably trips the watcher's regex engine and crashes the sidecar within seconds. ### Why it can look model-dependent Sessions that happen to create long paths crash; sessions that don't, never see it. This creates a false correlation between the crash and a specific model. The real variable is path length, not the model. ### Recommendations 1. **Upgrade or replace `@parcel/watcher`** to a release that resolves `parcel-bundler/watcher#250`. 2. **Bound/normalize path length** before passing paths to the watcher's glob-ignore matching, if upgrading isn't immediately possible. 3. **Add a config toggle to disable file watching** for users running file-intensive tasks. 4. **Graceful degradation:** when the sidecar crashes, preserve conversation state and allow reconnection without losing context. 5. **Long-path testing:** exercise the bundled native watcher with paths > 260 characters on Windows. ### Workaround (user-side) - Keep workspace file/directory basenames short. - Do file-intensive/intermediate work outside the watched workspace, then copy only short-named final artifacts into it. - Avoid printing long recursive path listings that the watcher may then process. ### Related - #29033 (open) — same exit code / `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` on Windows, root cause not identified - #28413 (closed, not planned) — same exit code `3221226505`

signals.title: Unexpected silent merge of opencode.json and opencode.jsonc — partial overrides without warning
signals.text: ### Description When both `opencode.json` and `opencode.jsonc` exist in the config directory, OpenCode silently merges them. A partial `.jsonc` can override specific keys from a full `.json` without any indication to the user. In my case, `opencode.json` had the correct MCP config for Engram: ```json "engram": { "command": ["/usr/local/bin/engram", "mcp", "--tools=agent"] } ``` But opencode.jsonc (leftover from a previous setup) had: ``` "engram": { "command": ["/usr/local/Cellar/engram/1.16.1/bin/engram", "mcp", "--tools=agent"] } ``` This caused a confusing ENOENT error pointing to a path that didn't exist (1.16.1), even though the .json file was correct. Expected Either: 1. Document the precedence/merge behavior clearly (which file wins when both exist?) 2. Warn when a partial config overrides specific keys from the other file 3. Or discourage having two config files with conflicting MCP entries Additional context The error message (ENOENT: no such file or directory, posix_spawn '/usr/local/Cellar/engram/1.16.1/bin/engram') didn't hint that the problem was a stale config file or a merge conflict — it looked like a missing binary. ### Plugins engram.ts, model-variants.ts, skill-registry.ts, gentle-logo.tsx ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json with a correct MCP entry: ```json "mcp": { "engram": { "command": ["/usr/local/bin/engram", "mcp"], "type": "local" } } ``` 2. Create ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc with a partial override of the same MCP server pointing to a non-existent path: ``` "mcp": { "engram": { "command": ["/usr/local/Cellar/engram/1.16.1/bin/engram", "mcp"], "type": "local" } } ``` 3. Launch OpenCode. 4. Observed: the MCP server silently fails with ENOENT. No warning that a second config file exists, no indication of the merge happening, and no hint about which file takes precedence. ### Screenshot and/or share link ### Operating System MacOS 26.5.1 ### Terminal iTerm2 Build 3.6.11
signals.author: escoffie

signals.title: Desktop: renderer unresponsive on startup — marked.js walkTokens synchronous Markdown AST traversal blocks UI thread
signals.text: ### Description OpenCode Desktop v1.17.7 on Windows 10 x64 crashes immediately after startup. The renderer process becomes unresponsive within ~60 seconds of launch, even without any user interaction — just opening the app and entering an existing project triggers the freeze. This is the same root cause as issue #30906 (renderer unresponsive due to synchronous CPU-intensive operations on the UI thread), but triggered through a different code path: Markdown AST traversal (marked.js walkTokens) rather than diff computation (Myers execEditLength). The app was auto-updated from v1.15.13 → v1.17.3 → v1.17.7. v1.15.13 worked fine; the regression started with the v1.16.0 Electron update. Key log evidence: window.log (16:33:49): renderer unresponsive { window: 'main', currentURL: 'oc://renderer/index.html' } Unresponsive samples (9 total) — all stuck in synchronous Markdown rendering: at B.walkTokens (main-BR8G9WSs.js:11645:5) ← marked.js sync AST walk at session-composer-state-C0aC1gfR.js:3396:20 ← Promise.all waiting → Markdown → PacedMarkdown → Show component chain ← SolidJS reactive cascade window.log (16:36:03) — second session, same pattern: renderer unresponsive after only 57 seconds of uptime at h → q → J → vn → heal → stream (session-composer-state) → Markdown component render via SolidJS createResource/createComputed manifest.json: uptime=69.88s — app killed within ~70 seconds server.log at crash time: global event disconnected Secondary (non-fatal) issues observed across all sessions: - @opencode-ai/plugin@local install failure (every 30-120s retry loop) - duplicate skill name: find-skills (3 locations) - ghostty-vt warning: unimplemented mode: 25 - Occasional fetch terminated errors to siliconflow API ### Plugins None (default installation, no custom plugins) ### OpenCode version v1.17.7 (auto-updated from v1.17.3, originally v1.15.13) Electron 42.3.3 / Chrome 148.0.7778.218 / Node 24.15.0 Windows x64, NSIS installer at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install OpenCode Desktop v1.17.7 on Windows 10/11 x64 2. Open an existing project with chat history (any project with prior sessions) 3. Wait 30-60 seconds — no interaction needed 4. Renderer becomes unresponsive, window freezes, process killed after ~10s watchdog timeout This happens on EVERY launch, not intermittently. The app is unusable. ### Screenshot and/or share link [window.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28980787/window.log) [window.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28980797/window.log) ### Operating System Windows 10 x64 (build 19045) ### Terminal N/A — using Desktop app, not TUI

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Improve slash skills menu — fuzzy search on descriptions, recently used skills, detail view
signals.text: - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ## Describe the enhancement you want to request Three small UX improvements to the `/` skills picker that make it easier to find and use skills: **1. Fuzzy search on descriptions** Currently the skills picker only matches on skill name/trigger. Searching also matches against descriptions so users can find skills by what they do, not just what they're called. **2. Recently used skills** Skills used in the last 30 days appear at the top of the picker (both TUI and web slash popover). Saves time when repeatedly using the same skills across sessions. **3. Skill detail view** `ctrl+o` in the TUI skills dialog expands a selected skill to show its full description and template content before inserting. Useful when you can't remember exactly what a skill does or what arguments it expects. All three are implemented and working on branch `skill-picker-upgrade` in fork https://github.com/Btema2/opencode — happy to adjust anything before a formal PR if the team has preferences.

signals.title: opencode Agent  config is silently ignored — opencode always sends  (1.17.7)
signals.text: **Title:** Agent `tool_choice` config is silently ignored — opencode always sends `tool_choice: "auto"` (1.17.7) ## Summary Setting `tool_choice` on an agent in `opencode.json` has no effect. opencode always sends `"tool_choice": "auto"` to the provider, regardless of the configured value. This is the exact capability requested in #14090 (closed as completed), but it does not work in 1.17.7 — the key is accepted without error and silently dropped. For models that don't reliably emit tool calls under `auto` (the failure mode #14090 itself describes for GPT), this makes autonomous/agentic sessions impossible: the model never gets asked to commit to a tool call, so the agent loop ends with no tool execution. ## Environment - opencode **1.17.7** (also reproduced on 1.17.4) - Provider: custom **OpenAI-compatible** (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`), local vLLM server - OS: Linux - Agent: `build` (default), invoked via `opencode run` ## Config used ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "provider": { "myprovider": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "options": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", "apiKey": "x" }, "models": { "my-model": { "name": "my-model" } } } }, "model": "myprovider/my-model", "agent": { "build": { "tool_choice": "required" } } } ``` ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider and set `agent.build.tool_choice: "required"` as above. 2. Run a tool-requiring task: `opencode run "Run the shell command: echo hello and report its output."` 3. Capture the outgoing HTTP request to the provider (e.g. `tcpdump -i lo -A 'tcp dst port 8000'`, since the provider is plaintext HTTP on loopback). ## Expected The request body sent to `/v1/chat/completions` contains `"tool_choice": "required"` (or the configured value), per #14090 and the Vercel AI SDK `toolChoice` parameter. ## Actual The request body always contains: ```json "tool_choice": "auto" ``` …even with `agent.build.tool_choice: "required"` set. No validation error or warning is emitted for the config key. The agent then receives a response with no usable tool call and the loop exits without executing anything. ### Wire evidence (captured with tcpdump on the loopback provider port) Request opencode sent (note `auto`, not the configured `required`): ``` "tool_choice":"auto" tools: bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, task, skill, todowrite, webfetch ``` Same request issued by hand with `"tool_choice":"required"` returns a valid tool call from the *same* model/endpoint, confirming the model and server are fine and the only difference is what opencode sends: ``` # tool_choice: "required" -> finish_reason: tool_calls, arguments: {"command":"echo hello"} # tool_choice: "auto" -> empty/again no usable call ``` ## Apparent root cause (from inspecting the 1.17.7 binary) - Every `tool_choice` schema in the bundle is a **provider request schema** (OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock/Gemini outgoing-request validation): `{model, messages, tools, tool_choice: optional(...)}`. - opencode's **agent config schema does not include a `tool_choice` field** (it's not alongside `prompt`/`model`/`temperature`/`mode`/`permission`). - The value sent derives from `ai.prompt.toolChoice`, which opencode's session/`streamText` path leaves unset → the AI SDK / provider defaults to `auto`. So the fix from #14090 (add `tool_choice` to the agent config schema and pass it into the `streamText` call) does not appear to be wired up in 1.17.7. ## Impact - No way to force `tool_choice: "required"` (or `none`, or a named tool) per agent. - Agentic use is unreliable on any model whose tool-calling is weak under `auto` — the documented motivation for #14090. ## Possible fix Wire the agent's `tool_choice` config through to the `toolChoice` argument of the `streamText` call (the AI SDK already supports `"auto" | "required" | "none" | {type:"tool", toolName}`), and add the field to the agent config schema so it validates. ## References - #14090 (feature request, closed completed) — the capability this issue reports as non-functional. - Vercel AI SDK `toolChoice`: https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/stream-text

signals.title: Desktop GUI freezes when prompt-history grows opencode.global.dat to hundreds of MB
signals.text: ### Description ## Description OpenCode Desktop became globally slow/unresponsive on Windows because the desktop global store file grew to ~370 MB, almost entirely from the `prompt-history` key. This affected the entire GUI, not just model responses. ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop version: 1.17.7 beta - OS: Windows - Install type: precompiled Desktop/Electron app - Plugins: none - Desktop store path: `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.global.dat` ## Symptoms The whole Desktop GUI became slow: - Opening/restoring the app from the taskbar was delayed. - Clicking buttons took several seconds to respond. - Opening menus was delayed. - Sending a prompt could appear to do nothing for 5-10 seconds. - The lag happened even when no model was actively working. - Because the UI lagged, clicking send again could accidentally hit stop/interruption. ## What I Found The desktop global store file was huge: ```text %APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.global.dat Size: 370,214,992 bytes # Temp Workaround $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop" $dir = Join-Path $env:APPDATA "ai.opencode.desktop" $store = Join-Path $dir "opencode.global.dat" $stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss" Copy-Item -LiteralPath $store -Destination "$store.$stamp.bak" -Force $script = @' const fs = require("fs") const file = process.argv[2] const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")) delete data["prompt-history"] fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(data, null, "\t"), "utf8") console.log("New file size:", fs.statSync(file).size, "bytes") '@ $script | node - "$store" ### Plugins NONE ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 beta ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use OpenCode Desktop on Windows with a long-running chat/session. 2. Send many prompts over time and pictures, especially large edit prompts, retried prompts, or prompts pasted through voice-to-text / Windows dictation. 3. Continue using the same workspace/session until the Desktop GUI starts becoming globally slow. 4. Observe that the slowdown affects the whole app: taskbar restore, menu opening, button clicks, and sending prompts all take several seconds. 5. Close OpenCode completely. 6. Check the desktop global store file: ```text %APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.global.dat ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows CMD

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Feature Request: Add GUI Options to Edit Custom Providers and Manage Model Lists
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Problem Statement Currently, managing custom providers (such as local inference engines like LM Studio or Jan AI) through the OpenCode UI is a destructive or highly technical process: No Edit Functionality: Once a custom provider is connected via the UI, the only available option is a Disconnect button. There is no way to modify existing fields like the baseURL or apiKey without fully disconnecting and re-entering all settings from scratch. No UI Model Management: Adding, removing, or adjusting configuration details (such as context and output limits) for specific models under a custom provider forces users to manually locate and edit the underlying opencode.json configuration file. While a "configuration-first" approach is excellent for project version control, a basic graphical CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) interface for connected providers and models would significantly improve the user experience, especially for users frequently swapping local models or modifying network ports. 💡 Proposed Solution Introduce an "Edit" action alongside the existing "Disconnect" button in the Providers settings UI, and add a dynamic schema viewer/editor for registered models. 1. Provider Edit Modal Change the single Disconnect button to an actions menu or place an Edit button next to it. Clicking Edit should open the initial connection modal with all existing fields (Provider ID, Display Name, Base URL, etc.) pre-filled with the current configuration data. 2. Inline Model Manager Under each connected custom provider in the UI, expose a list of currently registered models. Provide an "Add Model" button that opens a simple form to define: Model ID / Name Context Window Limit (to prevent the Context Limit 0 / empty usage bar issue) Output Limit Modalities (Text, Image, etc.)

signals.title: [BUG][Desktop vs Terminal] Pasting local file path has inconsistent behavior and no way to paste as plain text
signals.text: ### Description When pasting a local file path (e.g. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\image.png`) into opencode, the behavior differs between Desktop and Terminal, and **neither mode allows pasting the path as plain text**. ### Desktop App Behavior Pasting a local file path like `C:\Users\user\Desktop\image.png` automatically converts it to a file link (attachment reference). The path string itself is never sent to the model. ### Terminal (CLI) Behavior Pasting the same path automatically reads the file and embeds it as an image. The path string is again lost — the model receives the image content instead. ### Problem For users who use non-vision models (models that cannot process images), there is **no way to paste a local file path as plain text**. The intent is to let the AI see the path string itself (e.g., to ask it to copy the file, reference it in code, or describe what the filename means), not to embed the file content or create a link. ### Expected Behavior There should be a way to paste a local file path as **plain text** — for example: - A modifier key (Ctrl+Shift+V / Alt+V) to paste as raw text - A right-click context menu option "Paste as path" - Or auto-detection: paths wrapped in quotes or backticks are treated as text ### Environment - opencode Desktop (Windows) - opencode Terminal (Windows) - Both exhibit different behavior but neither supports plain-text path pasting ### Additional Context This is a combination of a bug (inconsistent Desktop vs Terminal behavior) and a feature request (need for a "paste as plain text" mode for file paths). The existing issue #32014 only covers the CLI side, but does not address the Desktop app or the inconsistency between the two. Related: #19892 (CLI only), #23458 (Ctrl+Shift+V works as plain text paste on Linux TUI but not documented/consistent).

signals.title: Remote MCP server using Streamable HTTP (Supabase) fails on Linux with SSE 405 in runtime — persists in v1.17.11
signals.text: ## Description Remote MCP servers that migrated to Streamable HTTP (POST-only) fail on Linux at runtime with `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`, even though the initial handshake succeeds. Reproduced with Supabase's hosted MCP (`mcp.supabase.com/mcp`, server v0.8.1). - `opencode mcp list` reports the server as `✓ connected` - `opencode mcp debug supabase-DEV` returns `HTTP response: 200 OK` and `Server info: supabase v0.8.1` - But in the TUI, the server keeps emitting `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)` This looks like the same root cause as #24946 (closed without a fix commit) and the open feature #28567. Filing a fresh report because it still reproduces on the latest release (v1.17.11) with a widely-used server. Note: #5636 (Figma 405) appears to be a different issue (client_name whitelist in dynamic OAuth), not a transport problem. ## Plugins None. ## OpenCode version v1.17.11 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure the Supabase remote MCP with a Bearer PAT (CI pattern from Supabase's own docs): ```json { "mcp": { "supabase-DEV": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=<project-ref>", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <personal-access-token>" }, "enabled": true } } } ``` 2. Start opencode and open the TUI → the server shows `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`. 3. `opencode mcp list` says `✓ connected`; `opencode mcp debug supabase-DEV` says `200 OK`. Direct curl against the endpoint with the same token: - `GET /mcp` → `405 Method Not Allowed` - `POST /mcp` with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` → `200 OK` So the server only speaks Streamable HTTP (POST); the handshake succeeds, but opencode's runtime transport keeps attempting GET/SSE. There's no way to force Streamable HTTP from config: the remote MCP `type` enum in `https://opencode.ai/config.json` is only `["remote"]` (no `"http"`/`"sse"` toggle). Supabase's docs show `"type": "http"` for clients that expose that field (Claude Code, Cursor, AI SDK), but opencode doesn't expose it. ## Screenshot and/or share link N/A (curl + `mcp debug` output above). ## Operating System Linux ## Terminal Alacritty

signals.title: Desktop Home view shows projects but zero sessions (database is correct)
signals.text: # Desktop (GUI) Home view shows projects but zero sessions — database is correct ## Summary The OpenCode Desktop app (macOS) shows the list of projects in the Home / sidebar, but every project displays **"Nothing here yet" / 0 sessions**, even though the SQLite database contains correctly-linked sessions. The terminal `opencode` CLI reads and writes the exact same database without any problem. ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop: **1.17.16** (also reproduced on earlier versions) - `opencode` CLI: **1.17.15** - OS: macOS (darwin, arm64) - Database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (~916 MB, 164 sessions, 5+ projects) ## Observed behavior 1. Open Desktop → Home view. 2. Sidebar lists the 3 projects the user has added (e.g. `opencode-settings-project`, `dockinkz`, `usage-widget`). 3. Selecting any project shows **"Nothing here yet — Create a session to get started"**. No session is listed for ANY project. 4. The terminal `opencode` CLI in the same projects works perfectly and its sessions are persisted to the DB. ## Expected behavior Sessions that exist in the database for a given project should appear in the Desktop Home view for that project. ## Evidence that the data is correct (not a DB/config issue) Verified directly against `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`: - `session.project_id` correctly references `project.id` (FK intact): ``` SELECT s.id, p.worktree, COUNT(*) FROM session s JOIN project p ON p.id = s.project_id GROUP BY p.id; -- /Users/diasmazhenov/vibecode/usage-widget | 3 -- /Users/diasmazhenov/vibecode/dockinkz | 1 -- .../opencode-settings-project | 1 ``` - `session.directory` matches `project.worktree` (fixed a mismatch, but the other projects already matched and still show 0). - `session.time_archived` is NULL for all relevant sessions. - `session.workspace_id` is NULL for all (consistent, not the cause). - `workspace` table is empty for everyone — not the differentiator. - The Desktop process holds the **same** shared DB file (confirmed via `lsof`: `OpenCode … /Users/diasmazhenov/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`). - Other projects (`/`, `open-design`) that are NOT in the Desktop sidebar DO have many sessions in the DB (86 / 73), so the Desktop's project list is a curated subset — but the 3 it shows still render 0 sessions despite valid data. ## Notes - The local Desktop API (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/project/:id/session`) returns `401 Unauthorized` (Basic realm) and the session list endpoint returns empty; the auth token could not be retrieved from local storage / process env, so the failure appears to be server-side session listing within the Desktop-embedded server rather than a pure frontend render issue. - A fresh restart of the Desktop app (which regenerates `opencode.global.dat`) does not resolve it. - `opencode serve` started manually also returns empty session lists for the same DB, suggesting the session-listing query/path used by the server is the failing component. ## Impact The Desktop GUI is effectively unusable for browsing/reopening past sessions; only the terminal CLI can access them. ## Root-cause analysis (from source) The Desktop Home session list pipeline: 1. `packages/app/src/pages/home.tsx` → `sessionLoad` query calls `focusedSync().project.loadSessions(directory, …)` for each `projectDirectories()`. 2. `packages/app/src/context/directory-sync.ts` → `fetch()` calls `client.session.list()` (SDK client scoped to the project directory) and stores results in the sync store. 3. `buildHomeSessionRecords()` (home.tsx:108) reads `sync.child(directory)[0]` and runs `sortedRootSessions()` → `roots()` → `isRootVisibleSession()`. 4. `packages/app/src/pages/layout/helpers.ts:26`: ```ts const isRootVisibleSession = (session, directory) => pathKey(session.directory) === pathKey(directory) && !session.parentID && !session.time?.archived ``` **The bug:** `isRootVisibleSession` reads `session.directory`, but the OpenCode server's `GET /api/session` response does **NOT** include a top-level `directory` field — the directory is only present under `location.directory`: ```json { "id": "ses_xxx", "projectID": "…", "location": { "directory": "/Users/…/project" }, "time": { "created": …, "updated": … } } ``` So `session.directory` is `undefined` → `pathKey(undefined) === pathKey(directory)` is `false` → **every session is filtered out** of the Home list. This matches the reported symptom exactly (projects show, sessions never do, for all projects). `projectForSession()` (helpers.ts:104) has the same problem: its directory fallback `pathKey(project.worktree) === pathKey(session.directory)` also fails when `session.directory` is undefined (only the `projectID` direct match works there). ### Suggested fix Either: - The server should return a top-level `directory` field on sessions (mirroring `location.directory`), or - The SDK/client `Session` type should map `location.directory` → `directory` before the UI consumes it.
signals.author: DiasMazhenov

signals.title: TUI dark/light mode does not follow Windows system theme
signals.text: ## Description On Windows 11 Terminal, when the user toggles the system dark/light mode (Settings > Personalization > Colors > Choose your mode), the terminal title bar changes colour but the terminal background colour (queried via OSC 11 `\e]11;?\e\`) does NOT change. Since opencode's TUI derives its dark/light mode exclusively from `terminalMode()` — which reads the terminal background colour — the TUI never detects the system theme switch and stays on the wrong colour mode. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Run opencode TUI on Windows 11 Terminal (Windows Terminal v1.20+) 2. Observe the TUI is in light mode (or dark mode) 3. Open Windows Settings → Personalization → Colors 4. Toggle "Choose your default app mode" between Light and Dark 5. The terminal title bar immediately reflects the change 6. The opencode TUI does NOT switch its colour mode ## Expected behaviour The TUI should follow the Windows system theme when running on Windows 11 Terminal, just like it follows the terminal background colour on other platforms/terminals. ## System info - Windows 11 - Windows Terminal 1.20+ - opencode dev branch ## Suggested fix Read the Windows registry key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme` as an additional signal. On Windows Terminal the background colour is not a reliable indicator of the system theme because the title bar and buffer background are decoupled.

signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Deepseek is now employing peak hour pricing as of today. So does Xiaomi. To keep costs low and load balance as Deepseek and Xiaomi want with this pricing, opencode can have a feature to automatically pause work within the peak hour window, when the model provider is deepseek or Xiaomi, or an API reseller such as opencode zen/go or openrouter using non free models. This would be useful when running long autonomous tasks such as a ralph loop with oh my openagent which do not require interaction with the user and can run unattented for several hours even while the user is sleeping, when given answers to common questions in the prompt. If work is started within the peak hour window, it could wait until the peak hour window is over before starting to do it. The feature could be turned on by default to avoid unexpected cost overruns with deepseek and can be optional with xiaomi since with xiaomi with this feature there would be only 8 off peak (productive) hours https://mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/tokenplan/Token%20Plan/subscription. whereas with deepseek there would be about 16 off peak (productive) hours daily. Since we don't know for sure whether an API is hosted by the provider or if the provdier is a reseller, this feature can be turned on by default based on model name. The user can be warned about peak pricing when they choose deepseek or xiaomi models which would be a UI change. The feature could use time zones to start and stop based on the user's local time. However this can be wrong so for reliability maybe it would be better to directly query UTC time via the network time protocol. The user should be able to override this feature and to be not asked again, when asked. I wonder if this is a better fit for oh-my-openagent given that i have only seen this issue with it installed because it can run for like 7 hours unattended but with opencode on its own it can sometimes run for like an hour unattended when asked to iterate until something is done or when asked to run in a loop and that can fall into peak pricing

signals.title: Windows paths from SSE clients not converted on Linux/WSL — corrupts database, crashes server, 100% WSL CPU
signals.text: **Related issues:** #16680, #15719, #27879, #30895, #33107 **Related PR:** #34256 ### Description Running `opencode web` or `opencode serve` inside WSL breaks as soon as a Windows browser or Desktop client connects. The SSE `/event?directory=` endpoint receives native Windows paths (`C:\Users\K\...`), but the path normalization function `windowsPath()` is a **no-op on Linux**. These raw Windows paths get concatenated with the server working directory (producing garbage like `/home/k/opencode/C:\...`) and written into the SQLite database. On restart, `Project.list()` crashes: `Path.isAbsolute("C:/Users/...")` returns `false` on Linux, and the code's fallback check is gated behind `process.platform === "win32"`. The resulting error/retry loop **saturates the WSL VM to 100% CPU**, freezing both the opencode server and the entire WSL environment. This makes `opencode web` / `opencode serve` in WSL completely unusable — the very act of connecting from Windows destroys the server's ability to function. #### Root Cause Two functions are platform-gated to Windows only: **`packages/core/src/fs-util.ts:147` — `windowsPath()`** skips conversion on Linux/WSL: ```ts export function windowsPath(p: string): string { if (process.platform !== "win32") return p // ... } ``` When a Windows client sends `?directory=C:\Users\K\...`, this function returns the path unchanged. `path.resolve()` then treats it as relative to CWD, producing `/home/k/opencode/C:\Users\K\...`. **`packages/core/src/database/path.ts:14-18` — `absolute()`** rejects Windows paths on Linux: ```ts function absolute(input: string) { const result = storagePath(input) if (!nodePath.posix.isAbsolute(result) && !(process.platform === "win32" && isWindowsStoragePath(result))) { throw new Error(`Path is not absolute: ${input}`) } } ``` The `isWindowsStoragePath()` function would correctly identify `C:/...` as valid, but it's never consulted because the outer `process.platform === "win32"` guard is `false` on Linux. #### Log Evidence ```log ERROR message=failed ref=err_a576f06d error="EffectDrizzleQueryError: Failed query: select ... from \"project\" (cause: Cause([Fail(Error: Path is not absolute: C:/Users/K/Documents/INFO)]))" ``` ```log INFO message="creating instance" directory=/home/k/opencode/C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode INFO message="fromDirectory" directory=/home/k/opencode/C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode WARN message="failed to initialize fff" error="Invalid path C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode" ERROR message="FileSystem.realPath (C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode)" error="ENOENT: no such file or directory" ``` ```log INFO message="global event connected" INFO message="creating instance" directory="/home/k/opencode/C:\\Users\\K\\Documents\\test-opencode" ``` ### Plugins none ### OpenCode version 1.17.20 (tested on Linux binary, WSL Debian, Windows binary) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install opencode inside WSL (Debian/Ubuntu), start `opencode web` with a clean state 2. Open `http://localhost:3030` in a **Windows** browser (or use Windows Desktop with remote server configured to WSL) 3. Immediately — within seconds of the browser loading — the SSE `/event?directory=` endpoint receives the frontend's native Windows path: ``` ?directory=C:\Users\K\Documents\my-project ``` 4. Server's `windowsPath()` is a no-op on Linux. `path.resolve()` treats it as relative to CWD: ``` → "/home/k/opencode/C:\Users\K\Documents\my-project" ``` 5. Server logs `"creating instance" directory=/home/k/opencode/C:\Users\K\Documents\my-project` 6. `Project.fromDirectory()` writes the garbage path to SQLite `project` table 7. `FSUtil.resolve()` immediately fails with `ENOENT` on `realPath(C:/Users/K/...)` because the path doesn't exist on Linux 8. FFF initialization fails with `"Invalid path C:/Users/K/Documents/my-project"` 9. Server enters tight error/retry loop — keeps attempting operations on the garbage path → **WSL VM spikes to 100% CPU within seconds** The problem manifests on the very first Windows client connection. ### Screenshot and/or share link none ### Operating System Windows 11 host, WSL2 Debian guest (Linux kernel via wsl) ### Terminal WSL terminal (Debian), `opencode web` process

signals.title: Vertex AI multi-region location (us/eu) produces invalid hostname
signals.text: ### Description When the Vertex AI provider's `location` is set to a continental multi-region value like `us` or `eu`, opencode builds an invalid API hostname: Invalid hostname: us-aiplatform.googleapis.com Only `global` is treated as not needing a region prefix on the hostname; `us` and `eu` need the same treatment (they're multi-region, not single-region like `us-central1`). This affects both the OpenAI-compatible endpoint template in opencode's own code, and the native @ai-sdk/google-vertex SDK call (which has the identical "only special-cases global" bug baked into its own default baseURL). I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.18.1 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure the google-vertex provider: "provider": { "google-vertex": { "options": { "project": "", "location": "us" } } } 2. Select a Gemini model 3.
