signal.title: tui: prompt and steer selected subagents
signal.text: ## Problem The V2 TUI can select a child Session, inspect its live activity, cycle between children, and interrupt one child without affecting its siblings. The selected child inspector is read-only, however: the composer remains owned by the parent Session. This makes the most useful recovery loop impossible when one of several parallel subagents starts going in the wrong direction: 1. Inspect the problematic child. 2. Interrupt only that child if necessary. 3. Send it corrective instructions. 4. Let that child resume with its existing context while every sibling continues. Today the user can perform steps 1 and 2, but not step 3 from the child inspector. ## Current V2 surface The compact TUI already has the right selection boundary: - `session.child.first` opens the subagent picker. - Selecting a child opens its read-only inspector. - `composer.subagent.interrupt` interrupts that selected child Session. - `Tab` cycles through child Sessions. - `Esc` returns to the parent composer. Selection currently changes only the observed child transcript. It does not retarget prompt submission. ## Proposed interaction When a child is selected, show a composer whose target is explicitly that child Session: ```text ◔ Inspect session execution Explore ctrl+d interrupt 1 of 5 Search "SessionExecution" Read packages/core/src/session/execution.ts I’m tracing the ownership path... ┃ Message Explore... ``` ### Soft steer Submitting while the child is running should admit a prompt to the selected child with `delivery: "steer"`. ```text select child → type correction → submit → correction is promoted at the child’s next safe step boundary ``` The active provider request or tool is not cancelled. Sibling Sessions are unaffected. ### Hard redirect The existing targeted interrupt remains available: ```text select child → interrupt selected child → type correction → submit → child wakes with the correction and retained history ``` The interrupt must affect only the selected child. Prompt submission after interruption must target that same child Session, not the parent. ## Existing V2 capabilities This should not require a new child-specific protocol: - Child agents are real Sessions with stable Session IDs. - `POST /api/session/:sessionID/prompt` already supports durable admission, `delivery: "steer" | "queue"`, and wake scheduling. - `POST /api/session/:sessionID/interrupt` already targets one Session. - A steer can be admitted while the child is running and promoted at its next safe model-step boundary. The primary missing piece is TUI target routing and presentation: the selected child must become the composer target while the inspector is open. ## Prior art Claude Code’s in-process teammate view is the closest interaction: selecting a teammate replaces the visible transcript, `Esc` interrupts only that teammate’s current work, and the normal composer submits into that teammate’s pending-message queue. The teammate resumes with retained history while siblings continue. Grok Build allows inspecting and individually cancelling a subagent, but its child view is intentionally read-only. Current Codex V2 allows inspecting and interrupting a parent-owned child thread but disables direct child input; follow-ups are mediated through the parent. Older direct-input-capable Codex threads instead route the composer to the active child thread and use steer-or-start semantics. ## Gang grill Decisions to pressure-test before implementation: - Should Enter in a running child always mean `steer`, or should the normal parent default of queueing active-turn submissions remain consistent? - Is the inspector composer visibly distinct enough to prevent accidentally prompting the child instead of the parent? - After a targeted interrupt, should the inspector remain open and focused on an empty child composer? - Should there be an atomic “interrupt and send” operation, or is interrupt-then-submit sufficient? Ordering matters because interruption clears an advisory pending wake unless continuation is requested. - Can completed and failed children be continued from the same inspector, or only running/interrupted children? - Should child composer drafts be preserved independently when cycling with `Tab` or returning to the parent? - How are child permission and form requests represented while the user is directly viewing that child? - Does direct human prompting change parent ownership or completion-notification semantics? - Should the parent agent receive an explicit durable fact that the human redirected its child, or is that derivable from child history? - Is this interaction intentionally human-only, or should the parent also gain a first-class tool for steer/follow-up against an existing child Session? ## Acceptance criteria - A selected child inspector exposes a composer clearly labeled with the child target. - Submitting from that composer sends the prompt to the selected child Session ID. - A running child can receive a soft steer without interrupting its current physical attempt. - An interrupted, idle, or completed child can be continued with retained history, subject to the decisions above. - Interrupting or prompting one child does not interrupt, prompt, or otherwise mutate sibling Sessions. - Returning to the parent restores the parent composer and its draft. - Cycling between children cannot send a draft to the wrong Session. - API failures are shown in the child inspector rather than silently dropping the correction. - Tests cover target routing, soft steer, interrupt-then-prompt, child switching, and sibling isolation. ## Related - #41667 requests direct prompting of child sessions in web/desktop. - #38966 requests per-subagent steer/cancel/abort across parent tools and TUI. - #36423 tracks V2 subagent resume and steering compared with V1.

signal.title: fix(core): unify patch path resolution
signal.text: ## What Unify the V2 patch tool's path and permission resources with the canonical `LocationMutation` service already used by write and edit. ## Before / After **Before:** Patch resolved paths privately. Internal resources were project-relative, paths outside a nested Location but inside its project skipped external approval, external approval reused its boundary as the saved resource, and move destinations rebuilt permission data independently. **After:** Every hunk source and move destination resolves through `LocationMutation` as a file mutation. Internal resources are Location-relative, external resources and saved approval boundaries follow the canonical service, and source/destination permission metadata remains attached to the same sequential approval flow. ## How - Inject `LocationMutation.Service` into `PatchTool.Plugin` and reuse `LocationMutation.Target`. - Resolve and authorize source and move targets through one local operation with `kind: "file"`. - Honor an explicit file kind lexically instead of inspecting an existing target to select its approval boundary. - Derive edit-permission targets from prepared changes rather than maintaining parallel mutable state. - Keep the existing lexical lock keys, preparation order, edit approval, sequential mutations, formatting, and partial-application reporting. - Extend tests for nested Locations, explicit file-kind semantics, canonical external save boundaries, sibling paths outside the Location, and external move destinations. ## Scope - No changes to `FileMutation` design or patch atomicity. - No changes to patch operation ordering, formatting, approval cardinality, or partial-failure behavior. - V2 core only; no V1 `packages/opencode` changes. ## Testing - `bun run test test/tool-patch.test.ts test/location-mutation.test.ts` (50 passed) - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core` - Pre-push hook: `bun turbo typecheck --concurrency=3` (33 tasks passed) - `bunx prettier --check src/tool/plugin/patch.ts test/tool-patch.test.ts` ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR P[Patch hunk] --> L[LocationMutation.resolve] L --> X[external_directory approval when needed] L --> E[edit approval] X --> E E --> M[Locked sequential mutation] ```

signal.title: fix(mcp): fail loudly on MCP server config missing type
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #41229 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Many MCP config JSON objects written for Claude Code setup don't carry fields like `type` and `enabled` which Opencode uses. Previously, if you tried to configure an MCP server without a `type` field, Opencode would start, but you were not be able to load or use the MCP, and you wouldn't know why without going in and looking at the logs. This diverges from other validation behavior, for example for the `enabled` field, which fails loudly when malformed. Additionally, if you tried to configure a server without both `type` and `enabled`, you would get a CLI error indicating that the `enabled` field is missing, when really, you could configure an MCP server without `enabled` just fine. However, we want to be able to define standalone MCP entries that ONLY have the "enabled" field, which serve to override the global config where the startup commands etc are actually defined. The old Info object also matched an entry containing `enabled` against a loose `Schema.Struct({ enabled: Boolean })`, so entries like `{ "command": [...], "enabled": true }` were silently treated as directory-level overrides (whereas if other fields like "command" are being defined, this is an outer-level server definition that should be flagged as malformed). #### Changes - Add a `BareEnabled` schema declaration that strictly matches exactly `{ "enabled": boolean }` (so only actual override entries are treated as such) - Annotate the `expected` value of `type` so the error is more informative in telling the user what the value of the field should be ### How did you verify your code works? - *Unit tests*: Added unit tests covering: entry missing `type`, entry missing `type` but with `enabled`, malformed entry with `type`, and a valid bare `{ "enabled": boolean }` override. - *Local tests*: Tested CLI locally, changing and removing MCP config's "type" and "enabled" fields. If "type" is not specified on a non-override entry, opencode will now fail to start and emit an error rather than failing silently and failing to load MCP server(s). ### Screenshots / recordings ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: desktop: newly discovered Git project remains No Git after project inventory desync
signal.text: ## Summary OpenCode Desktop can permanently show **No Git** for a newly opened Git repository even though the server has correctly resolved the repository, persisted the project with `vcs: "git"`, started watching `.git/HEAD`, and fetched the current branch. The observed failure is a project-state synchronization issue, not Git discovery. The directory child store learns the repository project ID and VCS branch, but `sync().project` can only resolve project metadata through the independently bootstrapped global project inventory. If that inventory predates project discovery and the global event stream is disconnected, the new project never enters the frontend inventory. `sync().project` remains `undefined`, and the new-session UI maps that unresolved/loading state directly to `noGit=true`. This report is related to, but has a distinct user-visible failure mode from, #42532. The empty/global path bootstrap failures appear in the same run and make recovery less reliable; this issue focuses on the stale project inventory and incorrect **No Git** state after the repository itself has been successfully discovered. ## Environment - OpenCode CLI/sidecar: `0.0.0-next-17444` - OpenCode Desktop: beta build `0.0.0-beta-17453` - OS: macOS 26.5.2 (`25F84`), Darwin 25.5.0, arm64 - Shell: `/bin/zsh` - Terminal context: OpenCode Desktop Electron renderer; diagnostics shell reported `TERM=xterm-256color` - Install/channel: Desktop beta / `next` - Active plugins: none found - Source revision inspected: `4643e65ad6334de3e4e68dedc201d5fbb828c9fe` on `dev` ## Reproduction The exact timing dependency is important: the project must be new to the server's project inventory after the desktop has already bootstrapped its global project list, and the global event stream must fail to deliver the subsequent `project.updated` event. 1. Start OpenCode Desktop with the managed sidecar service. 2. Let the desktop bootstrap its global project inventory before the target repository has been opened/discovered by this server. 3. Add/open a valid Git repository in the desktop app. 4. Open a new-session draft for that repository. 5. Observe that the project selector displays the repository name, but the adjacent Git status displays **No Git** indefinitely. 6. Verify independently that the repository is valid and that the backend now knows it is Git: - `git -C <repo> rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeds. - `GET /api/project` contains the project with `vcs: "git"`. - Server logs show location services booted for the repository and a watcher on `<repo>/.git/HEAD`. - The desktop workspace persistence for this directory contains the current branch. Observed in this run with a freshly cloned repository at `/Users/<user>/repos/opencode` on branch `dev`. ## Expected Behavior Once project discovery resolves a directory as Git, all project consumers should converge on that state. At minimum: - `sync().project` should resolve to the newly discovered project. - The new-session status should display branch/worktree controls rather than **No Git**. - A disconnected/reconnected global event stream should refresh the global project inventory. - An unresolved project during bootstrap should be represented as loading/unknown, not confirmed non-Git. ## Actual Behavior The server and directory state converge correctly, but the global frontend inventory does not: ```text Filesystem Git state -> valid repository, current branch dev Server project resolution -> project ID <project-id> -> vcs = "git" -> directory = /Users/<user>/repos/opencode -> .git/HEAD watcher started Directory child state -> project = <project-id> -> persisted vcs.branch = "dev" -> persisted vcs.default_branch = "dev" Global frontend project inventory -> project <project-id> absent/stale DirectorySync.project -> Binary.search(globalProjects, child.project) misses -> undefined NewSessionWorkspaceController.project.git() -> undefined?.vcs === "git" -> false NewSessionView -> noGit = !false -> true PromptGitStatus -> "No Git" ``` The result is internally contradictory UI: the repository can be selected by name and the branch is known in the directory cache, while the Git indicator says **No Git**. ## Confirmed Server Evidence The shared sidecar run was `72fdf00f`. Paths below are redacted only for the local username. ### Repository discovery succeeds At `2026-08-14T23:54:40Z`, after the new-session draft was opened, the server correctly initializes the repository: ```text 23:54:40.788 watcher subscribe path=/Users/<user>/repos/opencode/.opencode 23:54:40.798 worktree refresh started projectID=<project-id> 23:54:40.824 location services booted directory=/Users/<user>/repos/opencode workspaceID=undefined 23:54:40.825 worktree refresh done projectID=<project-id> 23:54:40.834 watcher subscribe path=/Users/<user>/repos/opencode/.git/HEAD 23:54:40.834 watcher started path=/Users/<user>/repos/opencode/.git/HEAD backend=node ``` This rules out missing Git, an invalid clone, an incorrect selected directory, and failure in repository discovery. ### Backend project inventory is correct After discovery, `GET /api/project` returns: ```json { "id": "<project-id>", "canonical": "/Users/<user>/repos/opencode", "vcs": "git", "sandboxes": [] } ``` ### Directory VCS cache is correct The desktop persistence file whose storage checksum maps exactly to `/Users/<user>/repos/opencode` contains: ```json { "workspace:vcs": "{\"value\":{\"branch\":\"dev\",\"default_branch\":\"dev\"}}" } ``` Therefore the directory-scoped VCS request completed successfully at some point. This cached branch is not sufficient to prevent **No Git**, because the UI gives project metadata precedence. ### Global event delivery is absent during discovery The prior global event stream logged: ```text 2026-08-14T23:34:47.861Z global event disconnected ``` There is no later `global event connected` entry before or during project discovery at `23:54:40Z`, and no delivered `project.updated` entry for the newly discovered project. The server's `Project.fromDirectory()` path emits `project.updated`, but the frontend inventory did not receive/apply it in this run. ## Related Empty-Directory Bootstrap Failures The same desktop run repeatedly bootstraps instance-scoped APIs with an empty directory before the repository context is available. This is likely related to #42532 and may amplify the stale-state problem. At `23:54:01.974Z-23:54:02.002Z`, all of the following return HTTP 500 with `Error: Path is not absolute:` where the path is empty: ```text /api/mcp /api/mcp/resource /api/location /api/provider /api/model /api/model/default /api/reference /api/vcs /api/agent /api/project/current /api/command /api/permission/request ``` The retries recur at approximately +1s, +3s, and +7s and still use the empty directory. The repository is not correctly routed until approximately 31 seconds after the last retry. This is not itself proof that the repository child was seeded incorrectly, because these calls may originate from placeholder/global bootstrap state. It is nevertheless a violated API invariant and should not be ignored during root-cause analysis: ```text frontend placeholder directory "" -> directory-aware client/request -> server absolute path decoder -> HTTP 500 -> bootstrap retries exhaust ``` ## Code/Data Flow ### 1. New-session draft supplies the directory `ResolvedDraftRoute` keys and provides the subtree using the draft server and directory: - `packages/app/src/app.tsx:209-230` ```tsx <Show when={`${props.draft.server}\0${props.draft.directory}`} keyed> <ServerSDKProvider server={conn}> <ServerSyncProvider server={conn}> <SDKProvider directory={directory}> <DirectoryDataProvider directory={directory} server={serverKey}> ``` The persisted draft in this run contains the correct directory `/Users/<user>/repos/opencode`. ### 2. Directory sync starts from a child store `useSync()` resolves the child by `sdk().directory`: - `packages/app/src/context/sync.tsx:113-118` ```ts return createMemo(() => serverSync().ensureDirSyncContext(sdk().directory)) ``` The child initially has `project: ""`, then bootstrap assigns a project ID: - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts:152-173` - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts:204-223` - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts:300-310` The child separately persists branch metadata under `workspace:vcs`: - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts:156-164` - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts:255` - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts:275-279` ### 3. Directory bootstrap only stores a project ID `bootstrapDirectory()` first attempts to seed from the current global project list: - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts:361-365` - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts:185-187` ```ts const seededProject = projectID(input.directory, input.global.project) if (seededProject) input.setStore("project", seededProject) ``` If the inventory predates project discovery, no seed exists. The fallback calls `project.current`, but discards the returned project metadata and stores only the ID: - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts:413-417` ```ts input.api.project.current({ location: { directory: input.directory } }).then((project) => input.setStore("project", project.id), ) ``` This creates a dependency on a second, independently updated data source: the global project list. ### 4. `sync().project` joins child ID against global inventory - `packages/app/src/context/directory-sync.ts:72-76` ```ts get project() { const store = current()[0] const match = Binary.search(serverSync.data.project, store.project, (project) => project.id) if (match.found) return serverSync.data.project[match.index] } ``` The global list is loaded separately through `project.list()`: - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts:127-141` - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts:143-166` If the child has `<project-id>` but the global list is stale, this getter returns `undefined` even though `project.current` already returned a full Git project and the backend inventory now contains it. ### 5. Project events are the intended convergence path `Project.fromDirectory()` emits the updated project after persistence: - `packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts:213-310` - `packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts:133-140` ```ts yield* emitUpdated(result) ``` The app applies `project.updated` by inserting/updating the sorted global list: - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/event-reducer.ts:37-64` The listener wiring is in: - `packages/app/src/context/server-sync.tsx:530-572` - `packages/app/src/context/server-sync.tsx:633-647` When the global stream is disconnected and does not recover, this convergence path is absent. The child ID remains orphaned relative to the frontend inventory. ### 6. Unknown project state is presented as confirmed non-Git The new-session workspace controller defines Git status exclusively from the resolved global project: - `packages/app/src/pages/new-session/new-session-workspace-controller.ts:34-49` - `packages/app/src/pages/new-session/new-session-workspace-controller.ts:65-69` ```ts git: () => sync().project?.vcs === "git" ``` The view negates that boolean: - `packages/app/src/pages/new-session/new-session-view.tsx:51-55` ```tsx <PromptGitStatus branch={props.workspace.bar.branch()} noGit={!props.workspace.project.git()} /> ``` `PromptGitStatus` gives `noGit` precedence over a known branch: - `packages/app/src/components/prompt-workspace-selector.tsx:101-106` ```ts if (props.noGit) return language.t("session.new.git.none") return props.branch ``` Thus `undefined`, loading, orphaned project ID, and confirmed non-Git all collapse to the same UI state. ### 7. Project selector can mask the mismatch The project selector displays the first available project if its directory cannot match a current project: - `packages/app/src/components/prompt-project-selector.tsx:59-70` ```ts const selected = () => current() ?? input.controls().available[0] ``` This can display the expected project name while Git status is calculated from an unresolved directory child, producing a misleading internally inconsistent row. ## Violated Invariants 1. **A directory child project ID must resolve in the global project inventory.** The current architecture allows `child.project = X` while `globalProjects` has no `X`. 2. **Successful `project.current` data should not be discarded when it is newer than `project.list`.** The full project response already contains `vcs`, `worktree`, and other metadata. 3. **Global SSE reconnection must eventually reconcile the inventory.** Missing one `project.updated` should not leave permanent stale state. 4. **Unknown/loading is not non-Git.** `sync().project === undefined` is insufficient evidence to show **No Git**. 5. **An empty placeholder directory must not cross the API boundary.** It should be gated in the client or rejected as a typed request error before reaching absolute-path database codecs. ## Likely Fix Surfaces These are options, not a claim that all are required: 1. On successful `project.current`, upsert the full returned project into `serverSync.data.project` before assigning the child ID, rather than discarding all fields except `id`. 2. If a child project ID cannot be found in the global inventory, trigger a targeted `project.list` refresh or retain the `project.current` object as the directory's authoritative metadata. 3. Make the global event client reconnect reliably and perform a project inventory refresh on reconnect. `server.connected` already has refresh behavior, but it cannot run if the stream never reconnects. 4. Represent project Git state as `unknown | git | none`, or gate the Git label on directory bootstrap completion. Do not map `undefined` to **No Git**. 5. Only use the project selector fallback for display when the current directory is genuinely absent, and avoid presenting fallback project identity beside status derived from a different/unresolved directory. 6. Prevent `directory: ""` from constructing/activating a directory sync context or serializing into location-aware requests. ## Suggested Regression Tests ### App state convergence Add a test around `bootstrapDirectory` / `DirectorySync.project`: 1. Global projects initially exclude project `X`. 2. `project.current({ directory })` returns full project `X` with `vcs: "git"`. 3. Assert the child resolves project `X` without waiting for a separately delivered global event. ### Missed project event recovery 1. Bootstrap the global project list without `X`. 2. Simulate global event disconnect. 3. Discover/open directory `X` as Git. 4. Simulate reconnect or a child bootstrap completion. 5. Assert global inventory contains `X` and new-session Git status resolves to Git. ### UI unknown state For `NewSessionWorkspaceController` / `NewSessionView`: 1. Child status is `loading` or `partial`. 2. `sync().project` is undefined. 3. A branch may or may not be cached. 4. Assert the UI does not render **No Git** until non-Git status is positively known. ### Empty directory guard 1. Global path query is still loading and exposes placeholder `directory: ""`. 2. Assert no directory-scoped bootstrap requests are sent with an empty location. 3. Assert no server request reaches absolute-path decoding with `""` or `"global"` as a filesystem path. ## Additional Notes - Restarting the service/app was intentionally avoided while diagnosing so the original state and logs remained intact. - No database or service files were edited. - The local Git repository remained clean throughout diagnosis. - Manual API checks and filesystem checks consistently identified the repository as Git. - Related issue: #42532 covers the repeated `global`/empty absolute-path failures. This report captures the separate persistent state/UI consequence after a real Git repository is successfully discovered.

signal.title: GitHub Copilot provider shows zero models: all models return `model_picker_enabled: false`
signal.text: ## Summary On opencode 1.18.15 (Arch package), the `github-copilot` provider never appears in the model picker. `opencode auth login -p github-copilot` works (auth succeeds), but `opencode models github-copilot` returns "Provider not found", and `/models` in the TUI shows no Copilot models. ## Root cause In `packages/opencode/src/plugin/github-copilot/copilot.ts`, the `models()` hook returns only models where `result.pickerEnabled.has(model.api.id)`: ```ts return CopilotModels.get(...) .then((result) => { models = result.models return Object.fromEntries( Object.entries(result.models).filter(([, model]) => result.pickerEnabled.has(model.api.id)), ) }) ``` `pickerEnabled` (built in `models.ts:257`) is the set of models with `model_picker_enabled: true` in the API response: ```ts pickerEnabled: new Set([...remote].filter(([, item]) => item.model_picker_enabled).map(([id]) => id)), ``` GitHub's `GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` currently returns **`model_picker_enabled: false` for every single model** — even ones that are `policy.state: "enabled"` and fully usable. So `pickerEnabled` is always empty, the filter drops everything, and the provider surfaces zero models. ## Evidence Using a valid, freshly-authenticated Copilot OAuth token (device flow, `client_id=Ov23li8tweQw6odWQebz`): ``` HTTP 200, total models: 47 policy states: disabled: 18 | none: 23 (internal: copilot-search-*, exec-agent-*) | enabled: 6 model_picker_enabled=true: 0 ``` The 6 `policy.state: "enabled"` models (gpt-4o, gpt-5-mini, claude-haiku-4.5, gpt-4.1, mai-code-1-flash, mai-code-1.1-flash) pass the existing `usable()` check (`models.ts:207`), and chat completions against them work fine: ``` POST https://api.githubcopilot.com/chat/completions → 200, "Hi there! ..." ``` So the account/subscription is fine — the filter is the problem. Note: exchanging the OAuth token for a Copilot session token via `api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` and using *that* against `/models` returns **403**, so the session-token route is not a workaround either. ## Suggested fix Filter by the already-existing `usable()` predicate (`policy.state !== "disabled"` + has `max_output_tokens`/`max_prompt_tokens` + has `tool_calls`) instead of, or in addition to, `model_picker_enabled`. Either: - Return `result.models` (already filtered by `usable()` inside `CopilotModels.get`) without the `pickerEnabled` filter, or - Union `pickerEnabled` with the usable set. `model_picker_enabled` appears to be a deprecated/no-longer-reliable signal from GitHub's API. ## Workaround A local plugin overriding the provider's `models()` hook to return all usable models (same `usable()` criteria, no picker filter) restores all 25 available Copilot models: ```js // ~/.config/opencode/plugins/copilot-picker-fix.js export const CopilotPickerFix = async () => ({ provider: { id: "github-copilot", async models(provider, ctx) { if (ctx.auth?.type !== "oauth") return provider.models const base = ctx.auth.enterpriseUrl ? `https://copilot-api.${ctx.auth.enterpriseUrl.replace(/^https?:\/\//, "").replace(/\/$/, "")}` : "https://api.githubcopilot.com" const r = await fetch(`${base}/models`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${ctx.auth.refresh}`, "User-Agent": "opencode/1.18.15", "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2026-06-01" }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000), }) if (!r.ok) return provider.models const j = await r.json() const models = {} for (const m of j.data || []) { if (m.policy?.state === "disabled") continue const lim = m.capabilities?.limits if (!lim?.max_output_tokens || !lim?.max_prompt_tokens) continue if (m.capabilities?.supports?.tool_calls === undefined) continue const isMsg = m.supported_endpoints?.includes("/v1/messages") models[m.id] = { id: m.id, providerID: "github-copilot", api: { id: m.id, url: isMsg ? `${base}/v1` : base, npm: isMsg ? "@ai-sdk/anthropic" : "@ai-sdk/github-copilot" }, status: "active", limit: { context: lim.max_context_window_tokens ?? lim.max_prompt_tokens, input: lim.max_prompt_tokens, output: lim.max_output_tokens }, capabilities: { temperature: true, reasoning: true, attachment: true, toolcall: m.capabilities.supports.tool_calls, input: { text: true, audio: false, image: !!m.capabilities.supports.vision, video: false, pdf: false }, output: { text: true, audio: false, image: false, video: false, pdf: false }, interleaved: false }, family: m.capabilities.family, name: m.name, cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cache: { read: 0, write: 0 } }, options: {}, headers: {}, release_date: m.version.startsWith(`${m.id}-`) ? m.version.slice(m.id.length + 1) : m.version, } } return models }, }, }) ``` ## Environment - opencode 1.18.15-1 (Arch Linux package) - GitHub Copilot subscription: active (chat completions return 200) - OAuth apps tested: opencode's own (`Ov23li8tweQw6odWQebz`) and the VSCode Copilot app (`Iv1.b507a08c87ecfe98`) — same result either way

signal.title: [BUG] Bash tool subprocess killed with SIGKILL when stdout streams many small writes (e.g. pytest tests/)
signal.text: ## Title [BUG] Bash tool subprocess killed with SIGKILL when stdout streams many small writes (e.g. `pytest tests/`) ## Body ### Environment - OpenCode CLI, version from 2026 - Running inside WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) on Windows 11 - Default provider config (model details irrelevant) - Memory: 19 GB total, 17 GB free at time of failure (NOT an OOM) - Disk: 946 GB free (NOT a disk-full) ### Observed behavior When the bash tool (or any sub-agent invocation that uses bash) runs a command that emits **many small writes to stdout in rapid succession**, the subprocess is killed with exit code 9 (SIGKILL). The parent OpenCode process and the user session remain alive. ### Reproduction In a Python project with pytest tests: ```bash # DOES reproduce (kills with SIGKILL, exit code 9): pytest tests/ -m "not integration" pytest tests/infrastructure/test_foo.py # Does NOT reproduce (succeeds normally): echo "hello" for i in $(seq 1 30); do echo "line $i"; done pytest tests/ --collect-only -q pytest tests/infrastructure/test_fastapi_app.py # 23 tests, single file ``` ### Hypothesis The trigger is the **streaming write pattern**, not the output size or the command. Pytest emits one write per test (a "." or "F" character) plus a carriage-return progress bar. Other commands that emit a single large write at the end (echo, `--collect-only`) or fewer writes survive. ### Attempts to work around (all failed) - `-q` flag (quiet mode) - `--tb=line --no-header --no-summary` - `-p no:cacheprovider` - `python3 -u` (forced unbuffered — made it worse if anything) - Different providers/models in `opencode.json` - Different MCP server configuration ### Related upstream issues - #40439 — TUI sessions hang permanently: zombie git child under project-copy-refresh snapshot step - #35241 — fix(shell): three timeouts and an exit fallback for the bash tool hang class - #28780 — fix(shell): add timeout guards for pre-spawn pipeline and post-SIGKILL cleanup - #24077 — opencode (default mode) closes entire terminal window on Linux / i3wm The pattern matches #35241's "bash tool hang class" most closely. ### Impact Blocks any verification that requires running a full test suite through the bash tool. Workarounds: split tests into many small pytest invocations, or run verification outside of OpenCode entirely.

signal.title: Desktop WSL sidecar fails with ServeError when networkingMode=mirrored
signal.text: ## Description OpenCode Desktop's managed WSL server consistently fails to start when WSL2 uses mirrored networking. The Desktop recognizes the distro and native Linux binary correctly, but the sidecar exits before health checking with only: ``` Error: Unexpected error ServeError ``` This appears to be a port-allocation handoff issue in `packages/desktop/src/main/wsl/sidecar.ts`: `allocatePort()` reserves an ephemeral port on Windows, closes it, and then asks WSL to bind `0.0.0.0` on the same port. With `networkingMode=mirrored`, Windows and WSL share the port space, and the immediate WSL bind fails. I reproduced the same allocation sequence independently 8 times; all 8 attempts failed with the identical `Unexpected error / ServeError`. Starting the same WSL binary directly on a known free fixed port succeeds. ## Plugins None in the WSL config. ## OpenCode version Desktop and WSL binary: 1.18.3 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure `%USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig`: ```ini [experimental] networkingMode=mirrored dnsTunneling=true autoProxy=true ``` 2. Run `wsl --shutdown`, then start OpenCode Desktop. 3. Add an installed WSL2 distro as a managed WSL server. 4. Observe that the server repeatedly fails before becoming healthy. Desktop log: ``` wsl sidecar starting { id: 'wsl:Ubuntu-24.04', distro: 'Ubuntu-24.04' } wsl sidecar { distro: 'Ubuntu-24.04', stream: 'stderr', text: 'Error: Unexpected error' } wsl sidecar { distro: 'Ubuntu-24.04', stream: 'stderr', text: 'ServeError' } wsl sidecar failed to start { message: 'WSL server exited before becoming healthy (code=1 signal=null)' } ``` Control test that succeeds: ```bash ~/.opencode/bin/opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096 ``` Expected: the managed WSL sidecar starts while mirrored networking remains enabled. A possible fix would be to allocate the port from inside WSL, let `opencode serve --port 0` report its selected port, or retry when the cross-environment port handoff fails. ## Operating System Windows 11 25H2 build 26200.8875; WSL 2.9.3.0; Ubuntu-24.04 distro. ## Terminal OpenCode Desktop managed WSL server (reproduced independently from PowerShell).

signal.title: fix(tui): restore compaction model marker
signal.text: ## What Restore the small `Compaction · <model>` marker after a completed V2 TUI compaction summary. The regression is confirmed against the concrete V1 `v1.17.20` tag: V1 stored compaction summaries as assistant messages with `mode: "compaction"`, `agent: "compaction"`, and provider/model identity, so the standard assistant footer rendered the compaction actor and model. V2 moved summaries to a dedicated compaction message but dropped model attribution from that message and rendered only the divider and summary. ## Before / After **Before:** when automatic or manual compaction completed, `session.compaction.ended` carried the summary but not the resolved catalog model. The projected `SessionMessageCompactionCompleted` therefore had no model, and the TUI ended after the summary without the V1 marker. **After:** a successful compaction records its resolved catalog `Model.Ref` on the terminal event, projects it into the completed message, and renders `Compaction · <catalog model name>` below the summary. Historical V2 rows and events remain readable because the field is optional; when old data has no model, the TUI preserves the old display instead of guessing from current session state. ## How - `packages/schema`: add the optional model attribution to the completed compaction message and terminal compaction event contracts. - `packages/core`: carry the resolved catalog ref through automatic, overflow-recovery, and manual compaction, then project it into the completed message. - `packages/tui`: retain model attribution from live terminal events and render the marker with catalog-name lookup plus provider/model fallback. - `packages/client`: regenerate the Promise client contract. - Tests cover historical payload compatibility, durable projection, live TUI projection, catalog display names, and fallback labels. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Core as Compaction core participant Event as session.compaction.ended participant Projection as Message projection participant TUI Core->>Event: summary + resolved Model.Ref Event->>Projection: complete compaction message Projection->>TUI: completed compaction + model TUI->>TUI: render Compaction · model ``` ## Scope - No change to compaction triggering, prompts, model selection, or summary content. - No marker for running or failed compactions because no successful model-authored summary exists yet. - No backfill or guessed attribution for historical completed compactions that predate this field. ## Testing - `bun run test` in `packages/core`: 1278 passed, 6 skipped. - `bun run test` in `packages/tui`: 222 passed, 1 skipped, 2 snapshots. - `bun test` in `packages/schema`: 35 passed. - Focused reruns: core 19 passed, TUI 38 passed, schema 7 passed. - `bun typecheck` in `packages/schema`, `packages/core`, `packages/client`, and `packages/tui`. - Push hook: `bun turbo typecheck --concurrency=3`, 32 packages passed. - `bun run check:generated` in `packages/client`. - `bun run lint` completed successfully with existing repository warnings. - `bun run test` in `packages/client`: 25 passed; 2 unrelated baseline failures remain because tests expect the stale `server.mcp` group while the generated client exposes `mcp`. ## Demo No visual artifact is attached. I attempted a real simulated V2 TUI run through `terminal-control` with: ```sh opencode-drive start --visible --dev /Users/kit/code/open-source/opencode-compaction-marker ``` The simulation launcher exited with `Failed to start server` before its control socket became ready and before the TUI rendered, so there was no honest screen to capture. The full OpenTUI suite and focused live-event projection test cover the rendered data path without substituting a staged mock for an end-to-end demo.

signal.title: feat(provider): add dynamic model discovery for custom providers
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #13891, #29308, #28999, #25624, #23327 & #26863 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Right now, setting up custom OpenAI-compatible providers (like LiteLLM, LM Studio, etc.) is pretty tedious because users have to manually type in every single model ID. This PR adds dynamic model discovery so we can just pull the available models directly from the provider's `/v1/models` endpoint. **Backend (`packages/opencode`):** - **New discovery endpoint:** Added a `POST /provider/discover` endpoint. It takes the base URL (plus optional API key and headers) and fetches `{baseURL}/v1/models` server-side, returning either the model IDs or a safely typed error. - **Background auto-discovery:** If an `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` config provider has a base URL and key, we now fetch its models at provider-build time (following the same pattern as the gitlab discovery loader). Hardcoded config models still win, so discovery just gracefully fills in the gaps. - **Daily sync:** I set up a daily `Effect.forkScoped` schedule to re-run discovery in the background so new remote models show up without requiring an app restart. Errors are swallowed here so an unreachable endpoint won't tank the provider load. - **Shared logic:** Extracted the core fetch logic into `src/provider/discover.ts` (`discoverOpenAICompatibleModels` & `DiscoverError`), which is shared by both the UI endpoint and the background loop. *Implementation note on path resolution:* I made sure to handle subpaths correctly. If a user's base URL already contains a path segment (e.g., `https://host/api/v1`), I append `/models` to it. Using `new URL("/v1/models", base)` would otherwise strip the `/api/v1` prefix away. **Frontend (`packages/app`):** - Hooked up a "Load dynamically" button in the Models section of the custom provider dialog. - It calls `client.provider.discover` (via the regenerated SDK), parses the response, and automatically populates the model rows. signal.title: feat(opencode): per-tool execution timeout with abort + session recovery
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Related: #20096, #34888, #20216, #34022, #34960 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Tools (built-in and MCP) can hang the agent loop indefinitely when they wedge on a long-running or unresponsive process. This adds a configurable per-tool execution timeout that aborts the call and synthesizes a tool-result so the agent can continue instead of staying stuck on a `status=running` part forever. **Config surface** (all optional, in milliseconds, `0` disables): | field | scope | default | |---|---|---| | `experimental.tool_timeout` | global default | `600000` (10 min) | | `experimental.task_timeout` | `task` tool only | falls back to `tool_timeout` | | `agent.tool_timeout` | per-agent override | highest precedence | **Precedence:** `agent.tool_timeout` > `experimental.task_timeout` (task only) > `experimental.tool_timeout` > `DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` On timeout the runner fires an `AbortController` composed with the user's existing abort signal via `AbortSignal.any`, so both Esc interrupts and timeouts surface through the same `ctx.abort` path. The catch block synthesizes a tool-result with `metadata.timeout=true` and a message guiding the agent to retry differently. The underlying process may still be alive — the abort is a best-effort cleanup nudge, not a hard kill. **Related PRs:** #20103 covers the same feature area with the same config keys. That PR is from a different contributor and has been open for a while; this one is an independent implementation with a different approach (centralized `ToolTimeout.resolve` module, `composeSignals` helper, per-agent override surfaced on `Agent.Info`). Happy to collaborate or defer if maintainers prefer consolidating. ### How did you verify your code works? - `test/session/tool-timeout.test.ts` — 10 tests covering: default fallback, global override, per-agent override, `0` disable, task tool precedence, task_timeout fallback, non-task tools ignoring task_timeout, agent override beating task_timeout, and ToolTimeoutError message shape. - `bun typecheck` in `packages/opencode` — clean. - `bun test test/session/retry.test.ts test/tool/task.test.ts` — 49 pass, 0 fail. - `bun test test/session/llm.test.ts` failures are pre-existing (mock LLM server route mismatches causing 5s timeouts), confirmed by running the same suite on clean `dev`. ### Screenshots / recordings _N/A._ ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Rounded corners for TUI code blocks and input box
signal.text: ## Describe the enhancement you want to request Add optional rounded corners for the code-block panels and the input box in the TUI (opencode cli), configurable via theme or tui config. ### Why With a compositor that rounds window corners (e.g. Hyprland `decoration.rounding`), the rounded terminal frame clashes with the hardcoded square-cornered borders opencode draws around assistant code blocks and the input field. A rounded style would look consistent with rounded terminal windows. ### Details - The TUI renders these borders with hardcoded square box-drawing characters (`┌┐└┘`); the rounded variants (`╭╮╰╯`) are not present in the binary at all. - The theme JSON format only exposes colors (background, border, text, diff/markdown/syntax colors) — there is no border-style or corner-radius option. - `tui.json` similarly has no UI style option beyond `theme`. ### Proposal Support a border style (e.g. `"round"` / `"square"`) in the theme or `tui.json`, defaulting to the current square corners so existing setups are unchanged. Since the TUI is built on opentui, if the underlying renderer already supports rounded corners this may just be exposing an existing option. Environment: opencode 1.18.18 (opentui TUI), Linux/Hyprland.

signal.title: fix(app): avoid Suspense splash on session switch
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Fixes #36876 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? Removes a spurious `<Suspense>` trigger on every session switch. The session timeline resource was read directly in JSX as `{sessionSync() ?? ""}` (`session.tsx`). Reading a `createResource` in JSX subscribes the render to it and trips the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary — the app-level splash — on every switch, even though the resource resolves to `void` and renders nothing. This PR removes the JSX read and the now-unused local alias. `createResource` fetches eagerly from its source signal (`sessionID`), so the refresh still runs; only the spurious Suspense subscription is gone. > **Scope note:** an earlier version of this PR also removed `deferRender`. Upstream has since deliberately kept `deferRender` (paired with the `reviewPanelV2Rendered` latch) for first-paint deferral, so this PR has been reduced to only the still-valid `sessionSync` Suspense-read removal to stay aligned with upstream. ### How did you verify your code works? `bun typecheck` passes. signal.title: refactor(opencode): lazily load cli commands
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Optimize process startup speed. ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? This PR improves the opencode CLI startup path by lazily loading command modules instead of importing every command during process initialization. Previously, `packages/opencode/src/index.ts` imported all CLI commands eagerly, even when the user only ran one command, checked the version, or launched the default TUI. This made startup do unnecessary module loading work. The change replaces those static command imports with command-specific dynamic imports. The CLI now detects the requested command from argv and only registers the command needed for that invocation. It still loads all commands when required for help or shell completion generation, so command discovery behavior is preserved. This also moves heap initialization behind a dynamic import so that it is only loaded when the command middleware actually starts the agent process. ### How did you verify your code works? Footer focus still translated each rendered action back through `actionItems().indexOf(item)`, re-entering that selection-dependent memo while the session picker registered its actions and exposing an uncomputed value. ## Fix - Track focused footer actions by stable command name instead of positional index. - Initialize the option/selection graph before registering action bindings that can evaluate selection-dependent availability. - Clear focus when the command becomes unavailable rather than transferring it to a different action at the same index. - Add regression coverage for a focused action becoming disabled. ## Verification - `bun test --timeout 30000 --only-failures` from `packages/tui` (220 pass, 1 skip) - `bun typecheck` from `packages/tui` - `bun x prettier --check packages/tui/src/ui/dialog-select.tsx packages/tui/test/cli/tui/dialog-select.test.tsx` - OpenCode Drive: while a model response is streaming, `/sessions` opens the Sessions dialog without hitting the error boundary

signal.title: fix: TUI blank screen, empty provider list against v2 daemon
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42643 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Three fixes in `packages/cli/src/tui.ts`: 1. The CLI passed a no-op plugin host. Slots render nothing (not even their fallback children) until a host calls `setupSlots`, and the home and session screens are slot-wrapped, so the TUI stayed blank behind the provider dialog. The host now sets up slots and registers the built-in feature plugins. 2. `gracefulFetch` answered the TUI's v1 reads (`/provider`, `/config/providers`, `/agent`, `/path`, `/project/current`, `/session`, `/session/{id}/`, ...) with empty stubs. It now adapts them from the v2 API in the v1 shapes the TUI expects, and bridges the v1 writes: create and prompt map to the v2 session endpoints (agent and model switch first, then prompt), abort maps to interrupt. One gotcha: the SDK sends a Request whose body the passthrough fetch consumes, so the bridge clones it before fetching. 3. The event stream never worked at all: the SDK validates each SSE frame against the GlobalEvent schema, the daemon's internal event shape (data plus durable/location) fails it, and one bad frame kills the stream silently. The bridge rebuilds each payload as `{id, type, properties}` and projects the `session.next.*` events into the legacy `message.*` events the session view understands. Prompt admissions and text deltas map directly for streaming; anything else triggers a debounced re-read of the session, so tools and token counts converge on what the daemon persisted. Not bridged yet: permission and question prompts, file attachments in prompts (text only), todo and diff (no v2 endpoints, answered empty), shell and compaction timeline entries. A cold daemon can also bootstrap the TUI before the catalog loads, which shows the empty provider dialog once; restart clears it. ### How did you verify your code works? With `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, bun run `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, and the same with the compiled binary. Before: the provider dialog lists only "Other Custom provider" and esc shows a blank screen. After: home renders with a model selected, "Say PONG and nothing else." streams PONG back, and a read-tool prompt shows the running tool and then the answer, with token counts updating live. ``` git clone --branch fix-tui-42643 https://github.com/moedash/opencode /tmp/oc-pr-test cd /tmp/oc-pr-test && bun install cd packages/cli export XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/oc-pr-xdg/data XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/oc-pr-xdg/state \ XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/oc-pr-xdg/config XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/oc-pr-xdg/cache OPENAI_API_KEY="$(cat ~/.config/ai363/llm.key)" bun run src/index.ts ``` ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Auto-discover models from OpenAI-compatible providers
signal.text: ## Describe the enhancement you want to request OpenAI-compatible providers configured with a `baseURL` (e.g. llama-swap, Ollama, LM Studio) serve a `/v1/models` endpoint that lists their available models. Right now you have to list every model manually in `opencode.json`, which means the config goes stale every time you swap a model on the backend. This PR adds auto-discovery: on startup, OpenCode calls `GET /v1/models` for each `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider that has a `baseURL` and no statically configured `models`. It reads `id`, `name`, `context_length`/`max_context_length`, and `max_output_tokens` from the response. Manually configured models always win (non-destructive merge), and opt-out is `discoverModels: false` in the provider config. Discovery runs in parallel across providers with a 2-second timeout per request, so offline servers don't slow startup. Errors are swallowed silently. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

signal.title: [FEATURE]:Performance issue: Context cache invalidation when switching modes or during compaction
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request I am experiencing significant performance issues when using OpenCode with local LLMs (inference engines like vLLM or Ollama). The context cache prefix is frequently invalidated, forcing the engine to reprocess the entire conversation history, which is very slow on local hardware. According to technical analysis (e.g., tests conducted by the Nicefox YouTube channel), OpenCode breaks the cache for several reasons: Tool Switching: When switching between "Plan" and "Build" modes, the list of available tools changes. Since tools are part of the request prefix, this modification invalidates the cache. History Modification: Instead of only appending new messages, OpenCode sometimes modifies previous messages in the history (for example, adding/removing "system reminders" about the current mode). Any change in the middle of the message history forces a full reprocessing of the context. Compaction: The conversation compaction process does not seem to preserve the cache prefix. Expected Behavior: The tools and the system prompt should remain constant (or be managed incrementally) across different modes to allow the inference engine to reuse the cached prefix. Previous messages should not be altered once they are part of the context. Comment reproduire le bug ? Pour prouver que le cache est "cassé", vous pouvez suivre ce protocole expérimental décrit dans les sources : Préparation : Utilisez un moteur d'inférence local (comme vLLM) et, si possible, un proxy (comme LiteLLM) qui permet de voir si le préfixe de cache est réutilisé ou si le texte est "re-processé". Étape 1 (Mode Plan) : Démarrez une session en mode Plan et envoyez un message simple (par exemple : "Bonjour"). Notez le temps de réponse. Étape 2 (Bascule de mode) : Passez en mode Build et renvoyez un message (par exemple : "Peux-tu m'aider ?"). Observation : Vous remarquerez que le moteur d'IA doit analyser à nouveau toute la conversation car OpenCode a changé la liste des outils disponibles entre les deux modes, ce qui "invalide" le cache. Étape 3 (Vérification de l'historique) : Regardez les requêtes envoyées. Vous constaterez qu'OpenCode modifie souvent le contenu de votre premier message (en y insérant des rappels système au lieu de les mettre dans un nouveau message), ce qui change le "hash" du préfixe et casse le cache. Étape 4 (Compaction) : Continuez la conversation jusqu'à ce que l'outil déclenche automatiquement le compactage de l'historique. Vous verrez que le temps de traitement devient extrêmement long car l'intégralité du contexte est à nouveau recalculée.

signal.title: fix(opencode): compare messages by time.created, not id, in latest()/runLoop
signal.text: Fixes #42639 latest() and runLoop compared messages by id string, but IDs from Identifier.ascending() wrap around (Date.now()*0x1000 overflows the 6-byte timestamp field), so a fresh "msg_000..." sorts before older IDs. This made latest() pick a stale message and the run loop exit before processing new user input. Compare by info.time.created with id as tiebreaker, matching the existing (desc time_created, desc id) pagination ordering. ## Verification - bun test packages/opencode/test/session/message-v2.test.ts

signal.text: ### Description When opencode v1.3.2 TUI is launched inside **any** git repository directory, messages cannot be sent. The input field accepts text, but pressing Enter/Submit does nothing ? the message never gets processed. The same opencode instance works perfectly when launched from a non-git directory (e.g., `~/`). ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.3.2 (latest, confirmed via `opencode upgrade`) ### Steps to reproduce 1. `cd` into any git repository directory (existing or freshly `git init`'d) 2. Run `opencode` 3. Type a message and press Enter 4. **Result**: Nothing happens. Message is not sent or processed. **Workaround**: Run `opencode` from a non-git directory (e.g., `~`). It works correctly there. ## Expected Behavior Messages should be sent and processed regardless of whether the working directory is a git repository. ## Environment - **opencode version**: 1.3.2 (latest, confirmed via `opencode upgrade`) - **OS**: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 (Plow) - **Kernel**: Linux 5.14.0-284.25.1.el9_2.x86_64 - **Architecture**: x86_64 - **Git version**: 2.39.2.3 - **Desktop**: KDE (affects XDG config paths) - **Installation method**: curl install script ## Diagnostic Details ### Log comparison: Non-git directory (works) vs Git directory (broken) **Working case** (`~/`, non-git, `projectID=global`) ? log excerpt: service=default directory=/home/user creating instance service=project directory=/home/user fromDirectory ... service=provider init service=provider providerID=github-copilot found service=provider providerID=opencode found After sending a message, the full pipeline runs: `skill init ? provider init ? tool.registry ? session.processor`. **Broken case** (`~/ronin_mcp_tools/`, git repo) ? log excerpt: service=default directory=/home/user/ronin_mcp_tools creating instance service=project directory=/home/user/ronin_mcp_tools fromDirectory ... service=provider init service=vcs branch=ronin_mcp_tools initialized service=bus type=file.watcher.updated subscribing **The log ends here.** After sending a message (POST completes with status 200), the processing pipeline (`skill init ? provider init ? tool.registry ? session.processor`) never starts. ### Key differences in git directories 1. `service=file.watcher init` and `service=vcs branch=<branch> initialized` appear **only** in git directories 2. `service=bus type=file.watcher.updated subscribing` is the last log entry in broken sessions 3. `pstree` confirms no MCP child processes are spawned (MCP init is part of the stalled pipeline) 4. Session permissions remain at the initial `deny` state because `tool.registry` never runs to override them ### Verified this is NOT caused by: - Config file issues (reproduced with empty `{}` opencode.json) - Specific git repos (reproduced in `git init` fresh directories) - MCP server configuration (reproduced with no MCP config at all) - Network issues (non-git directory works perfectly on the same machine) ## Additional Context - `opencode debug config` shows correct configuration in both cases - `opencode mcp list` works correctly when run from git directories - Only the TUI message sending is affected; CLI subcommands work fine - The `file.watcher` and `vcs` services that initialize in git directories may be related to the pipeline stall --- ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 (Plow) ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: fix(prompt-input): don't steal caret/focus while the editor is focused
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes the desktop focus-steal / caret-reset bug reported in #41332. When the draft prompt is reassigned programmatically (e.g. a draft restore triggered while the agent is streaming), the `prompt.current()` reactive effect rebuilt the contenteditable DOM. Because `renderEditor()` clears and rebuilds the node tree, the caret collapsed to **position 0** and focus was yanked away from whatever the user was doing. On X11 the WM then raises the window ("pops to front"), matching the reported symptom. User typing was already safe (`mirror.input` short-circuits reconcile / `localInput` in v2), but programmatic draft changes during streaming were not. ## Changes - `packages/app/src/components/prompt-input.tsx` - Guard the `prompt.current()` effect so it skips the DOM rebuild while the editor is focused; re-sync the DOM from the store on blur (`handleBlur`). - The store stays authoritative — only the visual rebuild is deferred. - `packages/session-ui/src/v2/components/prompt-input/index.tsx` - Same guard on the `parts()` effect (the v2 composer had the same rebuild-on-change path). ## Test plan - [x] Typecheck passes (`tsgo`/`tsc --noEmit` in both packages) - [ ] Manual: start a long-running agent task, keep typing in the prompt input (and in a terminal pane) — caret should stay put and the window should not steal focus / pop to front while the agent streams. Note: I could not fully reproduce in CI; this targets the documented mechanism in #41332. Happy to adjust if maintainers can point at a more precise trigger. Closes #41332

signal.title: 48-bit ID timestamp wraparound on 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC wedges all pre-existing sessions (loop exits at step 0, prompts silently ignored)
signal.text: ### Description **All sessions created before `2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC` silently stop processing prompts** due to a 48-bit timestamp wraparound in the ID generator (`packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`). This is likely the root cause behind #42605 and a spike of "agent stops responding in an existing session" reports starting today. #### Root cause `Identifier.create()` encodes `Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` into **6 bytes** (48 bits): ```ts let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // ← only the low 48 bits survive for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } ``` `Date.now() * 4096` is a ~53-bit number, so the sortable prefix wraps every `2^36 ms ≈ 2.18 years`. The most recent wrap boundary was: ``` 1786706395136 ms = 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC ``` Before the boundary, ascending IDs were near the top of the range (`msg_ffd4…`); after it they restart near zero (`msg_000b…`). Any new user message in a pre-existing session now **sorts before the entire session history**. The v2 session loop, which picks up work by ID ordering, sees nothing new past its watermark and exits immediately: ``` level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_… step=0 level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_… ``` No provider call is ever made; the message is stored but never processed. Retrying, switching models, and `/summarize` all fail the same way. Sessions created entirely after the boundary work fine (all IDs post-wrap, internally consistent). #### Evidence (from two independent production sessions, v1.18.4) Session A — last processed message vs. newly posted prompts: ``` last assistant msg (Aug 13): msg_ffd4c8ecc001nKKJtMDUGfajRL new user msg (Aug 14): msg_000bcb6970013Jm92xkWhlZiOA ← sorts before all history ``` Verification of the encoding: the new message was created at `1786718762656 ms`; `1786718762656 − 1786706395136 = 12,367,520 = 0xBCB6A0` → matches the observed `000bcb6…` prefix exactly. Session B — same split within one session: ``` first msg (Aug 13): msg_ffb02725b001iqapSOS18lP6Rb new msgs (Aug 14): msg_0007f07f9001…, msg_000e4a4c2001…, msg_000ebffe9001… ``` Newest row in the `message` table is a `user` message with no assistant response; every prompt produces the step-0 loop exit above. Also note `Identifier.timestamp()` in the same file decodes post-wrap IDs to garbage (it assumes the full timestamp survived), so anything deriving times from IDs is silently wrong after the boundary too. #### Impact - Every session with history from before 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC is permanently wedged on current releases (reproduced on 1.18.4; #42605 reports 1.18.1). `id.ts` is unchanged at current HEAD, so the bug is still live. - Next wrap: ~October 2028, when it will happen again for all then-active sessions. #### Suggested fixes 1. Widen the encoded value (8 bytes removes the problem for ~570 years), with a migration/compat story for existing IDs, or 2. Seed the generator / the loop watermark from `max(message.id)` per session at instance init, so new IDs always sort after existing ones, and 3. Short term: detect the condition (new user message ID < session max ID) and either re-key the message or surface an explicit error instead of silently ignoring the prompt. ### OpenCode version 1.18.4 (also reproduced indirectly on 1.18.1 via #42605); `id.ts` unchanged at HEAD as of 2026-08-14. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Take any session with messages created before 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC. 2. Send a new prompt. 3. Observe: message row is written, log shows `loop step=0` → `exiting loop`, no model call, no response. (Equivalent synthetic repro: create a session, insert a message with an ID in the `ff…` range, then prompt normally.) ### Operating System Linux (server mode, headless); also reported on Windows 11 Desktop (#42605).

signal.title: fix(app): show directories in web project picker on open
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #39434 Closes #37961 Closes #37611 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? The web directory picker ("Open project") always shows "No folders found" on a fresh browser profile, so there is no way to add a first project in `opencode web` / `opencode serve`. Two independent causes in `createDirectorySearch`: 1. An empty filter is sent to fuzzy find (`/find/file`). Fuzzy find returns nothing for an empty query, and fff additionally refuses to index `$HOME` / filesystem roots — which is where the picker bases itself (`sync.data.path.home`) on headless servers. Result: the picker always opens empty. 2. The browse call `file.list({ location: { directory } })` omits the `path` query param, which the server requires (`FileListData.query.path: string`). The server answers `HTTP 400 "Missing key at [\"path\"]"` and the `.catch(() => [])` swallows it. This also breaks the commonly suggested workaround of typing a path into the picker on current versions. Fix: pass `path: ""` to `file.list`, and route empty filters to directory browse (`match(directory, "", 50)`) instead of fuzzy find. Typed non-empty filters still use `/find/file` — unchanged. ### How did you verify your code works? - Reproduced against a live `opencode serve` 1.18.9 instance: `GET /file?directory=<dir>` → HTTP 400; the same request with `path=` → 200 with the full directory listing. - Added unit tests: empty filter browses via `file.list` (asserts `path: ""` is sent and `file.find` is not called); a typed filter still uses fuzzy find. - `bun run test:unit` (packages/app): 694 pass / 1 fail — the failure is `i18n parity`, which also fails on pristine `dev` (pre-existing, unrelated). - `bun run typecheck`: clean. ### Screenshots / recordings None attached — verified at the API level (curl repro above) and with unit tests. Happy to record the picker if a maintainer wants one. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR Two notes: - I deliberately kept "What does this PR do?" tight and technical — the template warns that large AI-looking descriptions get ignored, and this is exactly the level of detail a maintainer needs. - The Closes #... lines will auto-close all three issues on merge; the commit message carries the same references as backup.

signal.title: fix(core): restore plan mode reminder after compaction
signal.text: ## Problem The plan plugin injects its `<system-reminder>` enter/leave notices as synthetic transcript messages, but compaction cuts the model-visible transcript at the latest completed checkpoint (`SessionHistory.messageRows` only loads `seq >= compaction.seq`). After a compaction while on the plan agent, the enter reminder vanishes from context: the model no longer knows it is in Plan mode, tries to edit, and gets hard-blocked by the tool hook with no explanation. ## Fix Subscribe to `session.compaction.ended` in addition to `session.created` / `session.agent.selected`. When compaction completes, look up the session's current agent and re-inject the enter reminder if the session is still on the plan agent. The reminder is admitted as a steer synthetic (`resume: false`), so it promotes at the next safe step boundary just like the existing reminders. The `reminder` helper becomes effectful since the compaction case needs `ctx.session.get` to read the durable agent; the existing enter/leave logic for created/selected events is unchanged. ## Tests New `test/plugin/plan.test.ts` runs the real plugin effect against a stubbed plugin context: - enter/leave reminders on agent switches (existing behavior, previously untested) - enter reminder re-injected after `session.compaction.ended` while on the plan agent - no injection after compaction when the session is on another agent ## Not covered here Revert/undo interactions (committed reverts delete reminder rows while `SessionTable.agent` stays put) are a separate known issue and intentionally out of scope for this PR.

signal.title: Run loop can never exit when message ids are not time-sortable (imported sessions loop until the provider 400s)
signal.text: ### Summary `SessionPrompt.runLoop` decides a turn is finished by comparing message ids as **plain strings**. That is only correct because opencode's own ids embed a timestamp. Any session whose ids do not sort chronologically — e.g. one produced by a third-party importer — can put the loop in a state where it never exits: opencode re-requests indefinitely, each request ending on an assistant message, which providers reject. On Anthropic the user-visible result is a generic `Unexpected server error`, with the real cause (`This model does not support assistant message prefill`) buried. ### Where `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, in `runLoop`: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // <-- lexicographic id comparison ) { yield* Effect.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": sessionID }) break } ``` `MessageV2.latest()` selects the "last" user/assistant the same way. The invariant this relies on comes from `packages/schema/src/identifier.ts`: ids are a 12-hex-char prefix encoding `timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter`, plus 14 random chars — so they sort chronologically as strings. Nothing validates that invariant at the `import` boundary, and it is not documented in the `SessionV1` schema. ### Reproduction 1. Import a session whose message ids are random rather than time-sortable (I hit this with [baton](https://github.com/Kaseban/baton), which emitted `msg_<uuid>`; a hand-written JSON with random ids reproduces it too). 2. Resume it and send any prompt. 3. The first request succeeds. opencode then immediately issues a second request with the assistant's own reply appended, and the provider returns 400. Captured with a forwarding proxy in front of the provider: ``` req 1: 1035312B -> 200 OK response: "stop_reason":"end_turn" + "message_stop" req 2: 1035378B -> 400 "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." ``` The first response is a clean, complete turn — `end_turn`, `message_stop` — and opencode continues anyway. Failure is probabilistic in session length, because ~2.6% of random hex ids sort above a freshly generated native id: | messages | P(at least one imported id outranks the live ones) | observed | |---|---|---| | 3 | ~8% | worked | | 6 | ~15% | worked once, failed once | | 423 | ~100% | failed every attempt | Ruled out by testing, in case they look like suspects: plugins (reproduced with `--pure`), missing `step-start`/`step-finish` parts (synthesised them, no change), unpaired `tool_use`, unsigned thinking blocks, and empty message content. It reproduces with a structurally valid history — I replayed the exact captured payload standalone and it returned 200. ### Suggested fixes Either would resolve it; the first is the smaller change: 1. **Order by `time.created`** (falling back to id) in the loop test and in `MessageV2.latest()`, instead of comparing id strings. 2. **Break on a terminal finish reason regardless of ordering** — if `lastAssistant.finish === "stop"` and there are no pending tool calls, the turn is over; the id comparison is then only a tiebreaker. Worth considering alongside: a continuation request that would end on an assistant message is invalid for providers that disallow prefill, so guarding that at the request-building layer would turn this class of bug into a clear error rather than a loop. ### Related - #38620 — same seam (replay 400 with thinking + tool use) but a different trigger (`message.error !== undefined`); does not cover id ordering. - #21326, #25774 — orphaned/dangling `tool_use`; also this area, different cause. ### Environment opencode 1.18.4 · macOS arm64 (container, linux/arm64) · Anthropic-compatible endpoint (LiteLLM), `claude-opus-4-8`, `thinking: adaptive`. ### Note on the provider side Not an opencode bug, but it made diagnosis much harder: when the upstream rejected the request, the gateway's fallback chain retried on models that do not support `thinking: adaptive`, so both the original and fallback errors were collapsed into one opaque message. Surfacing the provider's `error.message` verbatim in the session log would have saved a lot of time here.

signal.title: feat: optional `preview` on question tool options
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #40846 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds an optional `preview` to a question tool `Option`: a block of plain monospace text shown beside the option list, tracking whichever option is focused. An option without one behaves exactly as today. The problem it solves: when a choice is between things that are inherently visual — two layouts, two implementations of the same function, two config shapes — a one-line `description` can't carry the difference. So the model dumps every variant into its message text *before* asking, and the prompt then appears below with bare labels like `1. Split 2. Stacked`. The content and the choice get separated at the moment you need them together. This puts the comparison inside the prompt. Where the pieces are: - **Schema** — `packages/schema/src/question.ts` (and the v1 `QuestionOption`) carries the field, plus `normalizePreview` and `previewLayout`. - **Normalization at the tool boundary** — `sanitize()` in `packages/core/src/tool/question.ts` runs once on the way in: strips markdown fence markers, ANSI escapes and control characters, tabs to spaces, trims blank edges, and truncates past 2000 chars with a visible marker. Previews are dropped outright when `multiple: true`, since there's no single focused option for a pane to track. Doing this once at the boundary means no renderer has to defend itself against model output, and a preview can't fail the tool call — worst case it normalizes to `undefined` and the option renders as it does today. - **Layout** — `previewLayout()` derives every bound from the viewport, never from the content: rows are `height/3` clamped to 4–12, the list column is 42% of content width clamped to 24–48, and the two-pane layout only engages when an option actually carries a preview and both columns clear 24 columns. Below 80 columns it falls back to single column. Long lines clip instead of wrapping so ASCII alignment survives. This part is deliberate — #11367, #18673 and #11014 are all "the question UI outgrew my screen", and adding content to that prompt without bounding it would have made them worse. - **Surfaces** — the TUI prompt (`packages/tui/src/routes/session/question.tsx`), the `run` footer, and the web/desktop question dock. - **Tool description** — `question.txt` tells the model when *not* to reach for it; an unnecessary preview pane is noise. The field is additive and optional, so there's no migration and no event version bump — clients that ignore it render exactly as before. **One open question, carried over from the issue and still unanswered:** this targets `Question.Option` on `dev`. On the v2 line the question tool lowers into a `Form` and `toField()` maps options through `{ value, label, description }`, so a `preview` would be silently dropped there. `Form.Option` may be the better home — it would give every form previews rather than just questions. Happy to retarget if that's preferred. ### How did you verify your code works? New tests, all passing: - `packages/schema/test/question.test.ts` (19) — normalization (fences, ANSI, control chars, blank-edge trimming, truncation) and the layout bounds across terminal sizes, including the narrow single-column fallback. - `packages/core/test/tool-question.test.ts` (7) — `sanitize()`, including previews being dropped for multi-select. - `packages/opencode/test/tool/question.test.ts` (3). Also: full TUI suite passes (193 pass, 0 fail), `bun turbo typecheck` is clean across `tui`/`core`/`opencode`, and `oxlint` reports 0 errors on the changed files. Rebased onto current `dev` before opening. ### Screenshots / recordings ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
