signal.title: fix(opencode): support mise-managed upgrades
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #36572 ### Type of change - [X] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? OpenCode currently detects updates for mise-managed installations, but cannot apply them because mise is treated as an unknown installation method. This PR detects binaries installed through mise and asks mise which config selected the running version. It updates that exact config while preserving its pinned or fuzzy version format. If the source cannot be identified unambiguously, the upgrade fails without modifying or creating a config file. The existing installation detection sequence is intentionally preserved. On startup, the backend checks for updates while the TUI separately connects to the event stream and registers the listener that opens the update dialog. Returning `mise` immediately made the check complete before that listener was ready, so the one-shot update event was lost and no popup appeared. Keeping the existing sequence preserves current startup ordering; adding an explicit TUI readiness handshake would be the cleaner long-term fix, but felt out of scope here. Ambiguous sources fail rather than falling back to `mise install`, since installing without activating the target would misleadingly report a successful upgrade. ### How did you verify your code works? signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #33720 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `opencode serve` keeps one runtime per directory forever, retaining its plugins, watchers, LSPs, MCPs, and database handles. signal.title: fix(llm): send assistant text as input_text in OpenAI Responses requests (#42613)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #42613. When a conversation history contains an assistant text message, the OpenAI Responses (`/responses`) request body used: ```json {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]} ``` `output_text` is not a valid easy-input content part: per the official OpenAI schema (`openai-python` types), assistant easy-input messages accept only `str | input_text | input_image | input_file`. Real `api.openai.com` tolerates the non-conformant shape, but strict OpenAI-compatible servers validating with the official SDK types (e.g. a self-hosted Qwen server exposing `/v1/responses`) reject it with a 422/400 pydantic `ValidationError`, so switching a session to such a model fails. ## Changes - `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts`: - Remove the now-unused `OpenAIResponsesOutputText` schema. - Lower assistant text content as `input_text` in request bodies (`lowerMessages`). - `OpenAIResponsesInputItem` assistant schema now uses `input_text` parts. - `packages/llm/test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts`: update expected request bodies (`output_text` → `input_text` for assistant input messages). ## Notes The AI SDK path (`@ai-sdk/openai` `convertToOpenAIResponsesMessages`) emits the same invalid shape and would need a separate fix upstream (`vercel/ai`) to fix released builds. ## Tests ```sh bun test test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts ``` 54 pass, 0 fail.

signal.title: Message IDs wrap around, silently dropping new user input in sessions with history
signal.text: ### Description In a session with existing message history, a new user message can be silently ignored — the agent loop exits without processing it. Root cause: Identifier.ascending() IDs are NOT monotonic. packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts encodes `Date.now()*0x1000 + counter` into a 6-byte (48-bit) field: let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // only 48 bits `Date.now()*0x1000` (~7.2e15 in 2026) exceeds 2^48 (~2.8e14) by ~25x, so the high bits are truncated. A freshly generated "msg_000..." sorts before older IDs. MessageV2.latest() picks the latest message by `info.id > user.id` (string compare), assuming IDs are monotonic (its comment says so). After wraparound it returns a stale message; the run loop then sees `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` and exits, dropping the new input. Suggested fix: compare by `info.time.created` (a real ms timestamp) with id as tiebreaker, matching the existing `(desc time_created, desc id)` pagination ordering. ### Plugins N/A (default config) ### OpenCode version v1.18.15 (also confirmed on dev @ 5d0f866) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session and exchange a few messages (build up message history). 2. Wait until the 48-bit timestamp field wraps — current date (2026) is already in the wrap window, since Date.now()*0x1000 overflows 2^48. 3. Send a new user message in the SAME session. 4. Observe: the agent does not respond. The run loop logs "exiting loop" and the new input is never sent to the model. Reproduction is time-dependent (tied to the wraparound point of the 48-bit timestamp), so it is intermittent rather than on every message. A reliable way to reproduce without waiting: unit-test latest() with messages whose time.created increases but whose ids wrap (a fresh "msg_000..." after older "msg_0a8a..."). ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: feat(storage): add safe database maintenance controls
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Stacked on #36710 by @chubes4. Partially addresses #16101. Related to #37495, #34875, #36851, and #32093. ### Relationship to existing work This PR is stacked on #36710. Its first six commits are exact cherry-picks from that PR, with @chubes4's authorship preserved. Review here should focus on the three subsequent commits: the storage controls, parallel analysis progress, and destructive-maintenance gate. After #36710 lands, this branch will be rebased onto the updated `dev` branch and the duplicated commits will be removed. #36851 explores automatic database maintenance by enabling incremental auto-vacuum and running a full Vacuum when a database first opens. This PR instead keeps destructive maintenance explicit, backup-first, observable, and coordinated through a process-wide maintenance gate. #32093 adds database diagnosis and repair for corrupt or invariant-violating rows. That work is complementary: this PR focuses on storage analysis, replay-safe event-history compaction, backup, checkpoint, and Vacuum of otherwise valid data. ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [x] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds a **Settings → Storage** page for inspecting and explicitly maintaining the SQLite database used by the selected OpenCode server. The page reports database, WAL, allocated, and reusable sizes, then exposes separate actions to: - analyze replay-safe event-history compaction candidates; - create and verify a compact backup; - compact superseded message and part snapshots; - checkpoint and truncate the WAL when readers allow it; - Vacuum the database to return reusable pages to the filesystem. Each destructive operation has a confirmation step showing the relevant candidate count, logical payload, database size, reusable space, and estimated backup requirement. Long-running analysis and maintenance report live phase progress. Event compaction is conservative. It handles only known full-snapshot message and part events, verifies that the newest retained snapshot matches the current projection, preserves event IDs and aggregate sequence numbers, excludes events above the indexed high-water mark, and skips malformed or incompatible aggregates. Compact and Vacuum require a verified backup before changing the active database. A process-wide maintenance gate coordinates destructive work with the server. It drains admitted legacy and v2 session runners, shells, detached prompts, background jobs, and summary/prune tasks. New mutating requests receive a structured 503 response while maintenance is draining or exclusive. Reads, progress, interrupts, and permission/question control replies remain available where needed to avoid deadlock. Analysis runs against a consistent temporary snapshot and uses Bun workers. Local 1/2/4/8/24-worker validation produced identical results. Performance scaled through eight workers, while 24 workers were slower because of SQLite and memory-bandwidth contention, so production analysis is capped at eight. The motivating database contained durable full-object event snapshots in addition to current message and part projections. On a verified long-lived database, Compact + Vacuum reduced the active file from 9,387,085,824 bytes to 7,727,558,656 bytes, reclaiming 1,659,527,168 bytes (17.68%) while preserving projections, row counts, latest timestamps, and normal OpenCode startup. This does not automatically delete or archive sessions. The maintenance gate is process-local; a database should still be maintained by only one OpenCode server process at a time. ### How did you verify your code works? Fresh pre-PR checks: - storage formatting tests: 2 passed; - database maintenance gate, backup/Vacuum, and event compaction tests: 6 passed; - HTTP maintenance middleware, parallel analysis, and progress tests: 6 passed; - `git diff --check`: passed. Broader validation on this branch: - `packages/core`: 1,090 tests passed; - HttpApi coverage/auth/effect exerciser: 216/216 passed in each mode; - prompt/task suite: 77 passed, 1 skipped; - v2 session runner: 83 passed; - Core, OpenCode, generated SDK, client, and targeted app typechecks passed; - lint completed without errors. The full OpenCode suite completed with 3,245 passes, 22 skips, and one todo. The remaining failures were isolated to existing WSL/NTFS subprocess startup timeouts; rerunning the affected ACP and help coverage passed independently. No failure involved storage maintenance, HttpApi, session runners, prompt/task behavior, or the maintenance gate. ### Screenshots / recordings Captured against an isolated test database; no user sessions or working paths are shown. **Storage overview** ![Storage overview](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/romanilyin/b5001be622780558cba458a22a2f0764/raw/2a95df67268789791a96f9ed0af34e7db0cbdfa7/storage-overview.svg) **Analysis result** ![Storage analysis result](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/romanilyin/b5001be622780558cba458a22a2f0764/raw/4d8f1c44ab29781e1d943877eee1166aa40cb5c2/storage-analysis.svg) **Vacuum confirmation** ![Vacuum confirmation](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/romanilyin/b5001be622780558cba458a22a2f0764/raw/b267a0d03413f441d6e604ebc2ba50f458c2abc5/storage-vacuum-confirmation.svg) ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
